Vendor it at 4MB, but index it as 'test in 4.7 before relying on it' rather than as a safe default. The underlying argument — that Godot's CSV translation import is picky about the key column and BOM/encoding — is correct and worth capturing in the index even if the tool itself needs updating.

resources.name: csv-to-gettext-converter (Wiechciu)
resources.license_evidence: raw main/LICENSE.md: "MIT License\n\nCopyright (c) 2025 WCHC"
resources.asset_license_note: Code only.
resources.why: Bridges the internal (CSV, easy) and external (PO, what Poedit/Crowdin/professional translators expect) worlds. Without this, going professional on localisation means hand-writing PO files.
resources.teaches: Converts multi-language translation CSVs into gettext .po/.pot from inside the Godot editor, with no external toolchain.
resources.notes: Note Godot also generates .pot natively via Project > Tools > Localization > POT Generation; this covers the CSV-first direction.

resources.name: fontTools
resources.license_evidence: raw main/LICENSE: "MIT License\n\nCopyright (c) 2017 Just van Rossum"
resources.asset_license_note: Tool only, produces derivative fonts — the source font's licence (usually OFL) still governs the output.
resources.why: Shipping CJK is the single biggest build-size hit in localisation, and this is the tool that solves it. Installable from pypi (reachable here), so no vendoring needed.
resources.teaches: pyftsubset for cutting a CJK/Cyrillic font down to the glyphs our translations actually use, plus font inspection/merging — the standard fix for a 30MB font in a 60MB build.
resources.notes: OFL permits subsetting and modification but requires the licence ship with the font and (for Reserved Font Names) a name change on modification.

resources.name: coi-serviceworker
resources.license_evidence: raw master/LICENSE: "MIT License\n\nCopyright (c) 2021 Guido Zuidhof"
resources.asset_license_note: Code only.
resources.why: Web export is the cheapest distribution channel for an undecided team, and the #1 web-export failure is 'SharedArrayBuffer is not defined' on itch/GitHub Pages. This is the standard 1-file fix.
resources.teaches: A service worker that re-serves the page with COOP/COEP headers so SharedArrayBuffer (and therefore Godot's threaded web export) works on hosts where you cannot control HTTP headers.
resources.notes: Godot-specific fork nisovin/godot-coi-serviceworker (raw main/LICENSE: 'MIT License / Copyright (c) 2023 nisovin') pre-wires it into Godot's exported index.html — vendor that one too, it is also ~1MB. Alternative with zero JS: untick Thread Support in the web export preset.

resources.name: godot-export (firebelley)
resources.license_evidence: raw master/LICENSE: "MIT License\n\nCopyright (c) 2024 Firebelley"
resources.asset_license_note: Code only.
resources.why: Turns 'build all platforms' into a tagged push. Reading its action.yml is also the clearest documentation of headless export CLI flags (--headless --export-release <preset> <path>) that exist anywhere.
resources.teaches: A GitHub Action that installs a chosen Godot version + export templates, runs every preset in export_presets.cfg, archives each output and optionally attaches them to a GitHub Release.
resources.notes: Complements godot-ci rather than competing: this is Actions-native, godot-ci is Docker/GitLab-friendly.
resources.fetch_command: git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout --depth 1 --no-tags -b master https://github.com/firebelley/godot-export third_party/godot-export && cd third_party/godot-export && git sparse-checkout set --no-cone 'src' 'action.yml' 'LICENSE' 'README.md' 'examples' && git checkout
resources.rejection_reason: CAVEAT: this is a GitHub Action (TypeScript), NOT a Godot addon — it belongs in the index under CI/release tooling, and note the brief says CI tooling is the PARALLEL sweep's territory, so check for overlap before committing. The sparse set drops dist/ (4MB of committed compiled JS) from the 6MB clone / 5MB worktree, leaving ~1MB; that is correct if the value is reading action.yml for the headless export flags, but if anyone intends to actually RUN the action from a vendored copy they need dist/ too. Default branch master.

resources.name: rfxgen (raysan5)
resources.license_evidence: master/LICENSE: "zlib License. Copyright (c) 2014-2026 Ramon Santamaria (@raysan5). This software is provided \"as-is\"... Permission is granted to anyone to use this software for any purpose, including commercial applications, and to alter it and redistribute it freely".
resources.asset_license_note: Code only; zlib covers it. Sounds you export are yours.
resources.why: The best-maintained tool in the sfxr lineage (commits as of 2026-08) and the reference implementation of the .rfx sound format. Value here is for a HUMAN doing a deliberate sound-design pass with a GUI and immediate audition, complementing the headless generators an agent uses. zlib is one of the most permissive licences on our allowed list.
resources.teaches: The canonical sfxr/rfxgen parameter set and the .rfx file format, useful if we want a compact on-disk representation of generated sounds.
resources.notes: C application built on raylib — requires compiling and a display, so it CANNOT be driven headlessly by an agent in this sandbox. Index it as the human-facing counterpart to jsfxr/pyfxr, not as build tooling.

resources.name: Bfxr2
resources.license_evidence: main/LICENSE: "MIT License. Copyright (c) 2021 Stephen Lavelle. Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy of this software and associated documentation files (the \"Software\"), to deal in the Software without restriction".
resources.asset_license_note: Code only.
resources.why: The modern MIT-licensed JavaScript rewrite of Bfxr by its original author (increpare/Stephen Lavelle, of PuzzleScript fame), actively developed. Bfxr extends sfxr with mixing multiple sounds and a wider synthesis palette, so it produces richer results than plain sfxr presets. Correctly licensed and clonable, unlike the original.
resources.teaches: Extended sfxr synthesis (sound mixing, additional waveforms) beyond the base 8-bit model.
resources.notes: Supersedes increpare/bfxr, whose own readme says: "MAR 2025 UPDATE: Bfxr has been superseeded by javascript reworking Bfxr2". The original bfxr is Apache-2.0 (declared only via a URL in readme.MD, with no LICENSE file) and is ActionScript/AIR — use Bfxr2 instead. Bfxr2 is a browser app; I did not verify a headless Node path, so treat it as human-facing unless someone extracts its synth core.

resources.name: jfxr
resources.license_evidence: lib/LICENSE: "Copyright (c) 2014, Thomas ten Cate. All rights reserved. Redistribution and use in source and binary forms, with or without modification, are permitted provided that the following conditions are met..."; lib/package.json declares "license": "BSD-3-Clause"; README: "The code itself is under a three-clause BSD license; see LICENSE for details. Any sound effects you make are entirely yours to do with as you please". npm registry jfxr@0.13.0 also reports license BSD-3-Clause.
resources.asset_license_note: Code only; README explicitly confirms generated sounds are unencumbered.
resources.why: A well-regarded sfxr successor with a notably richer parameter model than jsfxr (harmonics and falloff, separate low/high-pass cutoffs with sweeps, flanger, two independent frequency jumps, compression and normalisation). Actively maintained. Worth indexing as the upgrade path if jsfxr's preset space proves too narrow.
resources.teaches: A more expressive SFX parameter model — harmonics, flanger, dual pitch jumps, per-parameter sweeps.
resources.notes: HONEST STATUS: I could not get a clean repeatable headless invocation. Its Synth DID compute and reach a Clip in one attempt, so headless use is achievable, but the API is callback-based (synth.doneCallback) and undocumented for Node — someone must write a small wrapper first. Also note the ROOT of the repo has no LICENSE file; the BSD-3-Clause licences live in lib/ and app/, so record the per-package paths when vendoring.

resources.name: godot-localization-editor (EthanGrahn)
resources.license_evidence: raw main/LICENSE: "MIT License\n\nCopyright (c) 2022 Danny Garay"
resources.asset_license_note: Code only.
resources.why: The standalone mode is the differentiator — it lets a translator who does not have Godot installed work on the same files. Keep as the second option next to VP-GAMES.
resources.teaches: Godot-4 fork of the well-known localization-editor-g3; works both as an in-editor plugin and as a standalone app so a non-programmer translator can edit our CSVs.
resources.notes: Pick one of the two localisation editors for daily use; index both so an agent can choose by 'in-editor' vs 'standalone'.
resources.fetch_command: git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout --depth 1 --no-tags https://github.com/EthanGrahn/godot-localization-editor third_party/godot-localization-editor && cd third_party/godot-localization-editor && git sparse-checkout set --no-cone 'addons' 'samples' 'LICENSE' 'README.md' && git checkout
resources.rejection_reason: CLAIM VERIFIED and this is one of only three items in the batch that actually targets our engine version — project.godot declares config/features=PackedStringArray("4.7"), matching 4.7 exactly (the others being ProtonScatter and Konado). Clone 4MB / 3MB worktree; addons is 2MB. The 'standalone mode for translators without Godot' differentiator is a README claim I did not exercise.

resources.name: itch-publish (KikimoraGames) + butler
resources.license_evidence: raw master/LICENSE: "MIT License\n\nCopyright (c) 2020 Kikimora Games"
resources.asset_license_note: Action code MIT; it downloads butler, which is itself MIT (itchio/butler, raw master/LICENSE: 'MIT LICENSE / Copyright (c) 2018 Leaf Corcoran and Amos Wenger, https://itch.io').
resources.why: itch.io is the default first storefront for an undecided indie project, and this is the MIT path to automating it. Recorded specifically because the more popular alternative is GPL and would violate our policy.
resources.teaches: GitHub Action wrapper around butler push for itch.io channels (html5/windows/linux/osx) with --userversion, so releases are one workflow step.
resources.notes: AVOID yeslayla/butler-publish-itchio-action — verified GPL-3.0 (raw master/LICENSE: 'GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3'), forbidden by our licence policy.

resources.name: apple-codesign / rcodesign (indygreg/apple-platform-rs)
resources.license_evidence: raw main/apple-codesign/LICENSE: "Mozilla Public License Version 2.0" (per-crate licence; repo root has no LICENSE file)
resources.asset_license_note: MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft: fine for a tool we invoke as a binary; flagged per policy. Still requires a paid Apple Developer account and certificate.
resources.why: macOS distribution is blocked without Developer ID signing + notarisation, and this is the only credible open-source way to do it in CI. Concrete unblocker for shipping to Mac at all.
resources.teaches: Signing and notarising macOS .app bundles/DMGs from Linux or Windows CI without a Mac — including stapling the notarisation ticket, which is what Gatekeeper actually checks offline.
resources.notes: Windows equivalent is Authenticode via signtool/osslsigncode plus an OV/EV certificate — without one SmartScreen will warn on every download.

resources.name: chickensoft-games/GodotEnv
resources.license_evidence: raw main/LICENSE: 'MIT License / Copyright (c) 2022 Chickensoft Games'
resources.asset_license_note: code only
resources.why: Local counterpart to setup-godot: a CLI that installs and switches Godot versions per project on Windows/Linux/macOS, so every developer and CI runs the exact same 4.7.1 build. Also manages addons declared in a manifest. Prevents the classic 'works on my editor version' .tscn churn.
resources.teaches: Treating the engine version as a pinned project dependency rather than a per-developer install.
resources.notes: Distributed as a dotnet tool, which is a dependency a pure-GDScript team may not want. Alternative: a checked-in script that downloads the pinned godot-builds zip.

resources.name: Game Levels Blueprint (dannygaray60)
resources.license_evidence: raw .../main/LICENSE -> 'MIT License\n\nCopyright (c) 2022 Danny Garay'
resources.asset_license_note: Editor plugin code only; no assets.
resources.why: Indexed as the minimal alternative to Metroidvania-System's map layer for teams that want only the room-graph authoring, not a whole framework. Godot 3 only, so it is a design reference rather than an install.
resources.teaches: An in-editor graph for laying out how level/room scenes interconnect, with unlimited connections per scene — a lightweight world-structure tool for non-linear games.
resources.notes: Superseded for practical purposes by KoBeWi/Metroidvania-System (MIT, Godot 4.6), which does this and more.

resources.name: Agones
resources.license_evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/googleforgames/agones/main/LICENSE -> "Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004 / http://www.apache.org/licenses/"
resources.asset_license_note: Code Apache-2.0. No assets.
resources.godot_version: n/a — engine-agnostic, talks to your headless Godot server binary via a sidecar SDK
resources.last_activity: actively maintained by Google for Games
resources.why: 'Read this before choosing' material for authoritative dedicated servers. If a team says 'we want an authoritative server for 100 concurrent matches', Agones is the Apache-2.0 answer for how those processes get scheduled and allocated on Kubernetes. Indexing it stops an agent from inventing a bespoke orchestration scheme.
resources.teaches: The lifecycle of a dedicated game server at scale: Ready/Allocate/Shutdown, fleets, autoscaling, and why game servers are stateful and cannot use a plain HTTP load balancer.
resources.notes: DECISION NOTE: massively over-engineered for an indie first launch. For under ~50 concurrent matches, a single VPS running N headless Godot processes behind a tiny allocator script is the right call, and you graduate to Agones only if you have a hit. Requires Kubernetes.

resources.name: Open Match
resources.license_evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/googleforgames/open-match/main/LICENSE -> "Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004 / http://www.apache.org/licenses/"
resources.asset_license_note: Code Apache-2.0. No assets.
resources.why: The reference Apache-2.0 matchmaking architecture. Worth one index entry so that 'how do we do skill-based matchmaking' has a permissively licensed, well-documented answer rather than a hand-rolled queue.
resources.teaches: Matchmaking as a separable service: tickets with arbitrary properties, pools, match functions and evaluators — the vocabulary for skill/latency/region-based matching.
resources.notes: DECISION NOTE: for a first game, Nakama's built-in matchmaker (Apache-2.0, already in your stack if you take nakama-godot) covers property-based matching with far less operational cost. Reach for Open Match only if you outgrow it.

resources.name: Quilkin
resources.license_evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/googleforgames/quilkin/main/LICENSE -> "Apache License / Version 2.0, January 2004 / http://www.apache.org/licenses/"
resources.asset_license_note: Code Apache-2.0. No assets.
resources.godot_version: n/a — sits in front of any UDP game server, including headless Godot/ENet
resources.why: The realistic indie answer to two problems people mislabel as 'anti-cheat': DDoS/IP-harvesting and traffic abuse. Apache-2.0, sits in front of any UDP server, requires no game changes. Include it so the anti-cheat index entry has something actionable rather than only 'don't bother'.
resources.teaches: UDP proxying for games: hiding real server IPs, token-based routing, per-packet filters, rate limiting and traffic metrics.
resources.notes: DECISION NOTE on anti-cheat for an indie team, since the index needs one: (1) make the server authoritative — validate every move, score and currency change server-side and never trust client-reported state; (2) never ship secrets or authoritative logic in the client, GDScript in a .pck is trivially extractable (see GDRETools/gdsdecomp); (3) put a UDP proxy like Quilkin in front to hide server IPs and rate-limit; (4) do sanity/telemetry checks on impossible inputs and ban server-side. Do NOT plan on kernel anti-cheat (EAC/BattlEye) — it is not realistically available or affordable to an indie team, and it is worthless if your server already trusts the client.

resources.name: godot_rl_agents — reinforcement learning for NPC behaviour
resources.license_evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/edbeeching/godot_rl_agents/main/LICENSE -> 'MIT License / Copyright (c) 2021 Edward Beeching'
resources.asset_license_note: Example environments use primitive/author art under repo MIT.
resources.why: The one credible free option if a concept calls for learned rather than authored behaviour — driving/flying agents, emergent physics-toy creatures. Honest relevance is low for most genres, but it is the only entry covering this axis and it is MIT and actively maintained.
resources.teaches: Wiring a Godot scene up as an RL environment (sensors, action spaces, reward signals) and training agents with Stable-Baselines3/Ray, then exporting an ONNX policy to run in-game.
resources.notes: Requires a Python toolchain alongside Godot. Index it; do not vendor unless a concept explicitly wants learned agents.

resources.name: GDQuest/gdscript-docs-maker
resources.license_evidence: raw master/LICENSE: 'Copyright 2020 GDQuest / Permission is hereby granted, free of charge...' (MIT text)
resources.asset_license_note: n/a
resources.why: REJECTED. Its own README states verbatim: 'It is for Godot 3. The tool does not work with Godot 4.' Last commit 2024-03-30. Recorded here so nobody re-proposes it. The Godot 4 replacement is built in: `godot --headless --path . --doctool OUT --gdscript-docs res://`, which I ran successfully and which produced per-class XML with brief_description/description/methods extracted from ## doc comments.
resources.teaches: nothing we need - superseded
resources.notes: Use the engine's own --doctool --gdscript-docs instead.

resources.name: Scony/godot-gdscript-toolkit (gdlint / gdformat)
resources.license_evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/Scony/godot-gdscript-toolkit/master/LICENSE -> "MIT License\n\nCopyright (c) 2019 Pawel Lampe".
resources.asset_license_note: Pure Python tooling, no assets.
resources.why: Every other item in this domain tells an agent what good GDScript looks like; this one mechanically verifies it, which converts written best-practice into something checkable in CI. It closes the loop with abmarnie's advice and the two skill packs. Also reachable via pypi.org (which is open to us), so installation is not blocked. Included here rather than left to the parallel sweep because it is the enforcement half of 'written best-practice material on static typing and style'.
resources.teaches: The GDScript style rules as executable checks (gdlint) and an opinionated formatter (gdformat), plus a parser/grammar an agent can reuse to reason about GDScript syntax. README documents every lint rule and the .gdlintrc configuration surface.
resources.notes: Vendor the repo for its documented rule set and grammar; install the runnable tool from PyPI (`pip install gdtoolkit`) rather than running from the checkout. A repo-root .gdlintrc should be a follow-up task once a code style is agreed.

resources.name: GODOT-VFX-LIBRARY
resources.license_evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/haowg/GODOT-VFX-LIBRARY/main/LICENSE -> 'MIT License / Copyright (c) 2024 Godot VFX Library'
resources.why: Closes the dissolve / force-field / status-effect gap in one drop, which is currently represented in the repo by exactly one demo shader (dissintegrate). 48 shaders including dissolve, energy_barrier, heat_distortion, burning, frozen, petrify, poison, invisibility, portal_vortex, outline_glow, flash_white, blink, shake_intensity, radial_blur, chromatic_aberration, water and water_surface, plus 35+ ready GPUParticles2D effect scenes. Actively maintained, MIT, self-contained under addons/vfx_library/.
resources.teaches: A worked taxonomy of combat-feedback VFX: how hit-flash, status overlay, dissolve-on-death and screen-shake shaders are parameterised so a gameplay script can drive them from one float.
resources.notes: Aimed at action games but every shader is genre-neutral. Has API_REFERENCE.md, which makes it agent-navigable.

resources.name: GDQuest godot-visual-effects
resources.license_evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/gdquest-demos/godot-visual-effects/master/LICENSE -> 'This project uses 2 licenses: 1. The demo's source code ... is available under the MIT license. 2. Art assets (image textures and 3D models) are [CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0]'
resources.asset_license_note: ART IS CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 AND FORBIDDEN. Full clone 24 MB; sparse code-only checkout measured at 1 MB / 83 files with no art.
resources.why: The fire/explosions/lasers/trails gap is total — the repo has none of these today. This is the reference open-source set (1285 stars) from GDQuest's VFX Secrets course. Same dual-licence trap as their other repos, same sparse fix.
resources.teaches: How explosions, lasers and trails are actually assembled in Godot — the split between particle process material, mesh/ribbon geometry and the shader that shades it.

resources.name: GDQuest godot-4-VFX-assets
resources.license_evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/gdquest-demos/godot-4-VFX-assets/main/LICENSE -> 'This project uses 2 licenses: 1. The demo's source code ... is available under the MIT license.'
resources.asset_license_note: ART IS CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 AND FORBIDDEN. Full clone 8 MB; sparse code-only checkout measured 1 MB / 98 files.
resources.why: The Godot-4-native successor to godot-visual-effects: 35 shader files plus particle examples and materials, already ported to Godot 4 rather than needing translation from 3.x. Directly serves the 'particle/process material tricks' sub-domain.
resources.teaches: GPUParticles2D/3D process-material configuration in Godot 4 specifically — the sub-domain the brief calls out and that no vendored resource covers.

resources.name: Godot 4 Color Correction and Screen Effects
resources.license_evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/ArseniyMirniy/Godot-4-Color-Correction-and-Screen-Effects/main/LICENSE -> 'MIT License / Copyright (c) 2025 Arseniy Mirniy'
resources.asset_license_note: MIT throughout, but Textures/ alone is 81 MB and Extras/ 19 MB of demo imagery. Vendor 'Materials and Shaders' + Scenes only.
resources.why: Colour grading is a listed gap (the repo has only the demo BCS/sepia one-liners). This is the most complete free grading toolkit for Godot 4 and the only one offering AgX and Panini. Caveat that lowers its score: it is authored as VisualShader .tres resources, so an agent cannot read the effect as text the way it can with GodotRetro's color_correction.gdshader — vendor it as a tool, not as a reference.
resources.teaches: Video-editor-style grading controls (lift/gamma/gain, AgX and other tonemappers, Panini projection, vignette, chromatic aberration) expressed as VisualShader resources.

resources.name: abmarnie/godot-architecture-organization-advice
resources.license_evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/abmarnie/godot-architecture-organization-advice/main/LICENSE -> "MIT License\n\nCopyright (c) 2023 abmarnie". Single licence, covers the prose and the bundled script_templates.
resources.asset_license_note: No art assets. Repo is prose + .gd/.cs script templates only.
resources.godot_version: 4.0+ (explicitly "Godot 4.0+", advice is version-agnostic and holds for 4.7)
resources.why: This is the single highest-value text in the whole domain for a team with no game yet: it is exactly the decision an agent has to make first ("where does this file go?"), it is one self-contained README, it is 48 KB, and it is unambiguously MIT with no asset entanglement. It also ships script_templates/ which drop straight into a new project. It aligns with — and explicitly cross-references — the official Best Practices chapter we already have in the vendored manual, so it acts as the opinionated layer on top of the neutral docs.
resources.teaches: How to lay out a mid-sized Godot 4 project: addons/ for third-party code with their licences, src/ vs scene-local assets, per-scene folders holding a scene and its exclusive resources, prefix-based search navigation, inherited-scene folder nesting, where globally-shared resources live, plus scene-structure and quality-of-life sections.
resources.notes: Repo language is reported as C# but the content is language-neutral prose; 263 stars. VENDOR (stable text) rather than distil — it is already condensed, and rewriting it would only lose the author's caveats about when NOT to apply the advice.

resources.name: kidscancode/godot_recipes (Godot 4.x recipe text)
resources.license_evidence: raw.githubusercontent.com/kidscancode/godot_recipes/master/LICENSE -> "MIT License\n\nCopyright (c) 2019 KidsCanCode". README.md carries both an MIT badge and a CC-BY 4.0 badge ("licensebuttons by" linking creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0), so the prose is CC-BY 4.0 — allowed with attribution recorded. Default branch is master; main 404s.
resources.asset_license_note: Vendor ONLY src-4/content (117 .md, 800 KB). A full clone is 747 MB: docs/ is 370 MB of built HTML and static_shared/ is 156 MB of images. The images are not needed for greppable text; recipe markdown references them by URL and the text stands alone. Record attribution: "Godot Recipes by KidsCanCode, CC-BY 4.0".
resources.godot_version: 4.x (src-4 tree is the Godot 4 rewrite; src-3 is the Godot 3 material and must be excluded)
resources.why: This is the answer to the brief's KidsCanCode question: yes, the source is on GitHub, yes it is MIT with CC-BY prose, and yes the 4.x text can be vendored. It is the best "how do I do X" corpus in plain markdown — an agent greps one directory and gets a working GDScript answer with context, which is precisely the one-hop property we want. Because the game is undecided, breadth across AI/UI/physics/audio is an asset rather than dilution.
resources.teaches: 117 short problem→solution recipes with full GDScript: chasing/fleeing AI, tilemap navigation, homing missiles, changing behaviours, floating combat text, heart containers, debug overlay, minimap, radial menu, cooldown buttons, direction indicators, node tree/_ready ordering, migrating from 3 to 4, plus a g101 beginner track and first-2D-game walkthrough.
resources.notes: Excluding src-3/ is deliberate — Godot 3 recipes would poison agent answers for a 4.7 project. If we ever want the Godot 3 half it should be DISTILLED (concepts only), never vendored as-is.

unreachable: COGITO upstream (canonical, ahead of every GitHub fork) — https://codeberg.org/Phazorknight/Cogito — MIT code; bundled assets Kenney/Quaternius CC0 + Philip Drobar MIT, with one CC-BY-NC audio file and two CC-BY audio files. Codeberg is blocked in this sandbox; use the frepiso GitHub fork to vendor and point humans here for updates.

COGITO — first-person immersive-sim template with a full interactable/inventory/attribute framework; https://codeberg.org/Phazorknight/Cogito — licence claimed MIT (UNVERIFIED: codeberg.org is blocked from this environment, licence could not be fetched). The most complete permissive immersive-sim starter that exists; re-verify from an unblocked network before using. Note a GitHub mirror may exist under Phazorknight — worth searching.

COGITO — https://codeberg.org/Phazorknight/Cogito — First-person immersive-sim template for Godot 4 (interactable objects, inventory, item/attribute system). Listed in godotengine/awesome-godot under 'Templates / Godot 4'. Hosted on codeberg.org which is BLOCKED in this sandbox, so licence could not be fetched and it CANNOT be vendored here; awesome-godot's inclusion policy implies a free/libre licence but that is NOT verified evidence — a human must confirm the licence at the source before use. Relevant if the team picks a first-person or immersive-sim direction.

CReverter (Composite Reverter) — memento-based undo/redo utility supporting composition; https://codeberg.org/svetogam/creverter — licence claimed MIT (UNVERIFIED, codeberg blocked). Would be the answer if we pick a builder/editor/puzzle genre needing undo.

CSConnector (Contextual Signal/Setup Connector) — dynamically find, set up and connect to descendant nodes through the scene tree; https://codeberg.org/svetogam/csconnector — licence claimed MIT (UNVERIFIED, codeberg blocked).

CSLocator (Contextual Service Locator) — register and find objects through the scene tree like localised singletons, a clean alternative to global autoloads; https://codeberg.org/svetogam/cslocator — licence claimed MIT (UNVERIFIED, codeberg blocked). Directly relevant to subsystem architecture for a genre-undecided codebase.

Console porting for Godot — no open-source path. Requires a licensed partner under NDA: W4 Games (w4games.com), Pineapple Works, Lone Wolf Technology. Budget and NDA reality-check only; do not plan Switch/PS/Xbox in-house.

Dawnlike 16x16 roguelike tileset (DawnBringer) — https://opengameart.org/content/16x16-dawnhack-roguelike-tileset — used by statico/godot-roguelike-example. opengameart.org is BLOCKED. NOT CC0: the tileset carries its own terms and that repo's author deliberately ships only a subset because full inclusion 'would be full redistribution'. Do not extend or redistribute it without a human reading the source page.

Escoria (point-and-click adventure framework) — https://github.com/godotengine/escoria — listed in awesome-godot as the Godot point-and-click/adventure framework. `git ls-remote` on godotengine/escoria-demo returned NOT CLONABLE (repo moved or removed), and awesome-godot itself annotates Escoria as '(Godot 2 and 3)'. === HARD LICENCE FINDINGS (act on these) ===
1. COGITO ships ONE CC-BY-NC audio file: `addons/cogito/Assets/Audio/641848_newlocknew_fireburn.ogg` ("FIREBurn_Fireplace... by newlocknew -- License: Attribution NonCommercial 4.0", quoted from docs/about.rst:93). It also ships two CC-BY files needing recorded attribution: `Alarm Siren.wav by mirkosukovic` (CC-BY 4.0) and `Running Water by Poyekhali` (CC-BY 3.0). Everything else is Kenney/Quaternius CC0 or MIT. Code is cleanly MIT.
2. COGITO upstream is on Codeberg (unreachable). Its old GitHub home `Phazorknight/Cogito` 404s. Four live GitHub forks exist; I compared them by clone: Witoldinio 2024-03-25 (71MB), nicholaskarlson 2025-01-25 (66MB), melvspacestudio 2025-05-21 (83MB), frepiso 2025-06-16 (83MB, Godot 4.4). frepiso is freshest and preserves the original `Copyright (c) 2023 Phazorknight` LICENSE — use it. AVOID `chasesnip3rpp/Cogito`: it rewrote the LICENSE to `Copyright (c) 2026 roger-6532`, stripping the original author. That is a laundered fork; treat as untrustworthy provenance.
3. REJECTED for no LICENSE file (public repo = no rights granted): `catprisbrey/Godot4-OpenAnimationLibraries` (README mentions no licence either), `xDellTog/root-motion`, `SHawkeye77/Platformer3D3rdPerson`.
4. `bukkbeek/GodotFPS-Template` is MIT in LICENSE but its README adds "you are prohibited to resell any asset originating from this project including 3D assets, VFX, SFX and animations" — an ad-hoc non-free restriction that contradicts the MIT grant. Link-only; do not vendor its art.
5. `ETdoFresh/kenney.nl` has NO repo-root LICENSE, but every one of its 128 pack folders carries Kenney's own `License.txt` reading "License: (Creative Commons Zero, CC0)". CC0 permits redistribution, so the mirror is legitimate — but vendor per-pack WITH that pack's License.txt, never the bare repo.
6. `KhronosGroup/glTF-Sample-Assets` has no root LICENSE (LICENSE/.md/.txt all 404 on main) and per-model licences vary from CC0 to restricted. Do not vendor; reference only.

=== ENGINE-STATE ANSWERS THE BRIEF ASKED FOR ===
PHYSICS (Jolt vs Godot Physics in 2026): Jolt was merged into the engine as a module in 4.4 (Mar 2025), and became the DEFAULT 3D physics engine for new projects in 4.6. On 4.7 a new 3D project is already on Jolt; existing projects keep their old setting until `physics/3d/physics_engine` is changed manually. The `godot-jolt/godot-jolt` GDExtension README now states verbatim: "As of Godot 4.4, this integration of Jolt Physics is built into Godot itself... this extension will be considered to be in maintenance mode going forward, where only bug fixes will be considered". VERDICT: do NOT vendor the GDExtension. Use built-in Jolt. The one residual reason to read the extension is that it exposes joint-interface extras (`JoltHingeJoint3D` etc.) the engine module has not fully reached parity on — check that if you need advanced joints.
RENDERERS on 4.7 (stable 2026-06-19): Forward+ is the desktop default; Mobile is now the recommended default for XR projects (4.7 added Vulkan subsampled images, which cuts bandwidth under foveated rendering); Compatibility remains the web/low-end target. 4.7 added HDR output (Windows/macOS/Wayland/iOS/visionOS, 2D and 3D) and AreaLight3D. GI: SDFGI got reduced flicker on moving lights plus fixes for a null-uniform-set error and for ignoring visual layers; LightmapGI got a probe-update-speed fix under Compatibility; the ray-tracing path got better static-geometry denoising and faster probe placement. Practical guidance for an undecided team: prototype on Forward+ with SDFGI (zero bake time, costs ~1-2ms and needs a fully dynamic scene), switch to LightmapGI before ship if the world is mostly static and you need Mobile/Compatibility to work at all — SDFGI and VoxelGI are Forward+ only.
ANIMATION best practice on 4.7: `SkeletonIK3D` is on the deprecation path; new work should use the `SkeletonModifier3D` family (LookAt, FABRIK/CCDIK modifiers, physical-bone modifiers) layered on top of AnimationTree output. Root motion still goes through `AnimationTree.root_motion_track` + `get_root_motion_position/rotation`, with per-axis capture. Retargeting is now first-class in the importer (bone maps / SkeletonProfileHumanoid), which is why the standalone `coquistudios/godot-animation-retargeting` module is mostly legacy — prefer the built-in path plus a Mixamo automation addon.
BLENDER->GODOT conventions: Godot's glTF importer reads name suffixes on meshes — `-col` (trimesh static body sibling), `-convcol` (convex), `-colonly`/`-convcolonly` (collision replaces the mesh), `-navmesh`, `-rigid`, `-vehicle`, `-wheel`, `-occ`/`-occonly` (occluder). Blender is 1 unit = 1 m and Godot matches, so keep scene scale 1.0 and apply transforms; -Z forward / +Y up is handled by the glTF exporter. Godot can also import raw `.blend` files directly by invoking a local Blender install (Editor Settings > filesystem/import/blender). FBX needs FBX2glTF and is best avoided — prefer glTF/GLB, which is also why the KayKit/Kenney `gltf` subfolders are the only ones worth vendoring.

=== SCOPE BOUNDARIES RESPECTED ===
Did not touch: godot-demo-projects, Maaack template, the three Kenney Starter Kits, beehave, phantom-camera, godot-open-rpg, Terrain3D, ShaderV. Did not stray into the parallel sweep's lanes (official docs, GDScript tooling/CI, general gameplay addons, codebases-to-study, 2D neon shaders). NOTE for the index owner: `godotengine/godot-docs` IS reachable over git even though docs.godotengine.org is blocked — the 3D rendering/GI/physics/Blender-conventions prose above lives in that repo under `tutorials/3d/`, `tutorials/rendering/`, `tutorials/physics/` and `tutorials/assets_pipeline/importing_3d_scenes/`. That is the parallel sweep's territory, so I flag it rather than claim it.

The art is the point for an undecided team — Kenney + KayKit + Quaternius together cover platformer, dungeon crawler, RPG, roguelite, racing, city-builder, tower-defence, hex strategy and space, all CC0 with zero attribution obligation.

Roles: Inter = primary UI (variable, opsz+wght); Noto Sans = wide-language-coverage UI fallback (variable wdth+wght, Latin/Greek/Cyrillic; add ofl/notosansjp for CJK, confirmed 200 OK); Roboto = neutral alternate; Space Grotesk = display/techy; JetBrains Mono = monospace/debug/console; Orbitron + Bungee = display/logo; Silkscreen, Pixelify Sans, Press Start 2P, VT323 = pixel/retro; Noto Emoji = monochrome emoji glyphs for UI.

Measured totals: glTF-Sample-Assets Models/ = 1396 MB; ETdoFresh/kenney.nl = 531 MB; PolygonalMind = 5945 MB; M3-org/retro3d-assets = 721 MB; M3-org/base-meshes = 205 MB.
