A vendored 3D asset floor of ~120 MB buys ~3400 models, two rigged-humanoid pipelines and a CC0 animation library. Vendor sparse, never whole.

LICENCE LANDMINES FOUND (the reason per-model verification was mandatory):
1. KhronosGroup/glTF-Sample-Assets has NO repo-level LICENSE. Licensing is per-model in Models/<Name>/README.md "## Legal", with SPDX texts in LICENSES/. I classified all 159: 81 CC0-only, 60 CC-BY-4.0, 7 NON-FREE. The non-free set is `BrainStem` (Poser EULA), `DamagedHelmet` (CC BY-NC 4.0 — the most-copied glTF test model in the world is NON-COMMERCIAL), `Duck` (SCEA Shared Source), `Sponza` (CryEngine Limited License Agreement), `EnvironmentTest` (Adobe Stock License), `DragonAttenuation`/`DragonDispersion` (Stanford Graphics Library terms). LICENSES/ also ships CC-BY-NC-4.0.txt and LicenseRef-CRYENGINE-Agreement.txt, confirming mixed content. Any blanket clone imports forbidden material.
2. `Fox` is mixed WITHIN one model: mesh CC0, texture+animations CC BY 4.0 — attribution required despite the CC0 tag.
3. Several CC-BY models are "CC BY 4.0 with Trademark Limitations" (LicenseRef-CC-BY-TM, LicenseRef-LegalMark-Cesium/Khronos/UX3D) — the Cesium/Khronos logos on `BoxTextured`, `CesiumMan`, `CesiumMilkTruck` are trademarks and must not ship in a released game.

REPOS REJECTED FOR NO LICENCE (verified 404 on LICENSE/LICENSE.txt/LICENSE.md/COPYING on both main and master): Miziziziz/Retro3DGraphicsCollection, M3-org/retro3d-assets (721 MB of redistributed itch.io packs; only 3 of 3940 files carry any licence text), madjin/100avatars (README never states a licence and says the rigs came from Mixamo), nanos-world/nanos-world-quaternius (also Unreal .uasset — useless to Godot), nidorx/matcaps (README states the original authors could not be traced — licence laundering), alvarognnzz/ambientcg-downloader.

MIXAMO, PLAINLY: Adobe Mixamo animations and auto-rigs are licensed to the account holder for use in their own projects. They may NOT be redistributed as a standalone asset library, which is exactly what vendoring into third_party/ would be. Do not vendor Mixamo output, and treat any third-party repo whose README says "rigged with Mixamo" as unclearable. Mesh2Motion is the redistributable substitute.

CAVEAT ON Mesh2Motion: vendor everything EXCEPT static/animations/CarnegieMellonAnimations/. That folder's readme.txt says "A small sample of FBX file from a larger library here https://rancidmilk.itch.io/free-character-animations" — third-party itch.io provenance not covered by the repo's own CC0 grant. The other 10 animation GLBs are the author's own and are covered.

PROCEDURAL GENERATION IS THE REAL BLOAT ANSWER. Material Maker (MIT, itself built on Godot) generates PBR texture sets from node graphs, so we can stop downloading texture packs entirely. gdTree3D generates trees, ProtonScatter and Spatial Gardener place foliage, godot-constraint-solving does WFC level assembly (it has a dedicated wfc-3d branch), godot_voxel generates terrain. Together these replace several GB of downloadable content with a few MB of code.

BLOCKED-HOST REALITY CHECK: kenney.nl, quaternius.com, polyhaven.com and ambientcg.com are all unreachable here, and I found no usable GitHub mirror for Quaternius, Poly Haven or ambientCG. Kenney is the exception — ETdoFresh/kenney.nl is a real, complete, CC0-stated mirror that single-handedly closes the "CC0 low-poly kit" gap (nature, city, dungeon, castle, space, pirate, racing, food, furniture, tower-defense, hexagon, minigolf, animated characters). HDRIs: none found on GitHub under a verifiable licence; the already-vendored godot-demo-projects PolyHaven HDRI plus Godot 4's ProceduralSkyMaterial/PhysicalSkyMaterial should cover us until someone with open network access fetches from polyhaven.com.

DECISION SPINE (put this at the top of the index entry for this domain — a wrong netcode choice is the most expensive mistake available here):

STEP 1 — Do you need real-time netcode at all? Many genres do not. Puzzle, roguelite, 2D platformer and card games often need only leaderboards + cloud saves (-> Supabase SDK or Nakama), or asynchronous/turn-based play (-> Nakama or Colyseus over WebSocket). Adding real-time netcode you did not need is the most common way indie multiplayer projects die. Decide this before anything else.

STEP 2 — Topology. Three choices, in ascending cost:
  (a) Peer-hosted / listen-server (one player is the host). Cheapest, no server bill. Needs NAT traversal (-> noray, or Steam/EOS relay). Host advantage and host-migration pain are real.
  (b) Dedicated authoritative server (headless Godot export, `godot --headless`). The only architecture with meaningful cheat resistance. Costs money and ops. See devmoreir4's run_headless_server.sh for the minimal pattern; Agones for the at-scale pattern.
  (c) Backend-hosted authoritative logic (Nakama authoritative matches in Go/TS/Lua, or Colyseus rooms). You do not run Godot on the server at all — good for turn-based/card/strategy, wrong for physics-driven action.

STEP 3 — Latency compensation. Three answers, and they are NOT interchangeable:
  - NONE (plain MultiplayerSpawner/MultiplayerSynchronizer). Genuinely fine for co-op, turn-based, party, slow-paced and LAN games at 2-8 players. Reference: devmoreir4 template (Godot 4.6). Start here.
  - CLIENT-SIDE PREDICTION + SERVER RECONCILIATION (netfox). The default for anything action-y with a server authority. Works with non-deterministic physics. Vendor netfox.
  - DETERMINISTIC ROLLBACK (Snopek godot-rollback-netcode). Only for small-session, latency-critical, fully deterministic games (fighting, precise 2D action). Requires abandoning Godot's physics and floats for fixed-point (sg-physics-2d) — this is a project-shaping commitment, not an addon you bolt on. Do not choose it before the genre is decided.

STEP 4 — Transport, constrained by platform. Godot's high-level MultiplayerAPI is transport-agnostic, so this is a late, cheap decision — which is exactly why you should build against MultiplayerAPI rather than hand-rolling packets:
  - Desktop/mobile default: ENetMultiplayerPeer (built in, UDP, reliable+unreliable channels).
  - Steam release: Steam networking via GodotSteam (Codeberg) or the MIT Expresso SteamMultiplayerPeer — gives you Valve's relay and NAT traversal free.
  - Cross-store / Epic: EOSG (MIT wrapper) — free lobbies, P2P and relay, works even off the Epic Store.
  - WEB EXPORT IS THE HARD CONSTRAINT: browsers cannot open raw UDP sockets, so ENet does not exist on web. You get WebSocketMultiplayerPeer (TCP; head-of-line blocking under loss; fine for turn-based/card/strategy) or WebRTCMultiplayerPeer (unreliable datagrams; the only web-viable transport for action games, but needs a signalling server + STUN/TURN). If web is even possible, design the transport layer around this from day one — retrofitting is painful. Also note the .NET/C# build of Godot does not support web export, so choosing C# quietly forecloses browser multiplayer.

WHAT IS "VENDOR THE CODE" vs "READ THIS BEFORE CHOOSING":
  VENDOR: netfox (the anchor of the whole domain), godot-rollback-netcode, noray, webrtc-native, nakama-godot, nakama-project-template, colyseus, EOSG, and the three templates (thegatesbrowser sparse, devmoreir4, BatteryAcid sparse).
  READ-BEFORE-CHOOSING: Nakama server, Agones, Open Match, Quilkin, GameNetworkingSockets, GodotSteam, NetfoxSharp, CSharpGodotTools/Template, Supabase SDK, GodotFirebase, sg-physics-2d.

ALREADY IN third_party/ — DO NOT RE-VENDOR, BUT CROSS-LINK FROM THIS DOMAIN'S INDEX:
  - third_party/godot-demo-projects/networking/ contains the canonical first-party examples: multiplayer_bomber (high-level MultiplayerAPI end to end), multiplayer_pong, webrtc_signaling (the reference WebRTC signalling server + client — this is the piece webrtc-native does NOT give you), websocket_chat/websocket_multiplayer, and the ENet/UDP chat demos. These should be the FIRST hop for any "how do I do X in Godot multiplayer" question.
  - third_party/godot-docs contains the official "High-level multiplayer" and "Exporting for dedicated servers" tutorials, which are the authoritative source on MultiplayerSynchronizer visibility/interest management, replication config, and the headless/dedicated-server export preset. Do not duplicate them.

INTEREST MANAGEMENT specifically: Godot has this built in via MultiplayerSynchronizer's visibility filters (set_visibility_for / add_visibility_filter / public_visibility) — see godot-docs plus netfox/examples/visibility-filtering. There is no third-party addon worth vendoring for it; the built-in mechanism plus a distance/room filter is the whole answer at indie scale.

VERIFICATION METHOD USED: every candidate was checked with `git ls-remote --heads` for clonability; licences were fetched with curl against raw.githubusercontent.com (trying main/ and master/ across LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt, COPYING) or, for GitLab and for repos whose licence file sits at a non-standard path, by an actual `git clone --depth 1 --no-tags` and reading the file on disk. Sizes are real `du -sm` on those clones (all clones deleted afterwards). Note for future sweeps: gitlab.com raw-file URLs return 404 through this proxy, but `git clone` from gitlab.com works — so GitLab licences must be verified by cloning.

TRAPS FOUND, WORTH RECORDING IN THE INDEX SO NOBODY REPEATS THEM:
  1. GodotSteam has left GitHub entirely. github.com/GodotSteam/* are all ARCHIVED and emptied down to a single readme.md that says "This repository has been moved to Codeberg". An agent searching GitHub will conclude it is abandoned. It is not — it is at codeberg.org/godotsteam/godotsteam, which is blocked here.
  2. SnopekGames/godot-rollback-netcode does not exist on GitHub under that name. The project is on GitLab, and the branch that matters is `main` (v1.0.0, Godot 4.6, June 2026) — NOT the `godot-4` branch, which is stale at 4.1/alpha7 and last touched Dec 2023. Cloning the wrong branch would silently give you three-year-old code.
  3. expressobits/steam-multiplayer-peer carries an author notice pausing development (Dec 2025) and redirecting to GodotSteam.
  4. gsioteam/godot-colyseus is Godot 3 only (project.godot config_version=4) despite a recent-looking repo timestamp; last real commit Sept 2023. Same trap with ikbencasdoei/godot-voip (config_version=4, Godot 3) and Hairic95/Godot-WebSocket-Multiplayer-Template (config_version=4, Godot 3) — all three were REJECTED for that reason after cloning, even though their MIT licences verified fine. Repo "updated_at" on GitHub is not evidence of Godot 4 support; always check project.godot.
  5. thegatesbrowser/godot-multiplayer measures 170 MB, 141 MB of which is prebuilt twovoip binaries whose upstream repo and licence I could NOT locate from this sandbox. Sparse-vendor around them.
  6. BatteryAcid's template is MIT for code but ships character art with no licence statement and no credits section — code and assets are licensed separately and an MIT repo does not launder unattributed art. Excluded the art.

domain_notes.domain: E — Audio: SFX, music, and the tooling to make them
domain_notes.notes:
HEADLINE: procedural SFX generation works in this sandbox, and it removes the "go find a sound" loop entirely. I test-ran three generators end-to-end and produced 24 valid RIFF WAV files. Evidence at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-GODOT-GAME/4397c16f-53af-55dd-84c8-672c4edfe26f/scratchpad/audio/out and .../outpy (deleted clones, kept outputs).

1) chr15m/jsfxr (Node, Unlicense/public domain, ZERO runtime dependencies — no npm install needed, just clone and require). WORKING. API is NOT the documented `sfxr.generate`; the module exports {sfxr, convert, parameters, Params, SoundEffect, waveforms} and the generator lives on the nested object:
   const lib=require('./sfxr.js'); const params=lib.sfxr.generate('pickupCoin'); const wave=lib.sfxr.toWave(params); fs.writeFileSync(f, Buffer.from(wave.dataURI.split(',')[1],'base64'));
   Presets: pickupCoin, laserShoot, explosion, powerUp, hitHurt, jump, blipSelect, tone, click, random. Also ships a CLI `sfxr-to-wav <b58> out.wav` which works (emits a Buffer() deprecation warning on Node 22 but still writes valid WAV). Params.toB58() gives a short reproducible seed string — ideal for storing a sound as one line of text in a repo instead of a binary.

2) lordmauve/pyfxr (Python, BSD-3-Clause). WORKING. `pip3 install pyfxr` succeeded (prebuilt wheel for Python 3.11 linux, no compiler needed). API gotcha: the SFX helpers return an SFX *params* object, not audio — you must call .build() first:
   pyfxr.pickup().build().save('x.wav')   # pickup/laser/explosion/powerup/hurt/jump/select
   pyfxr.tone('E4').save(...) and pyfxr.pluck(duration=1.0, pitch='A4').save(...) work directly (these return SoundBuffer). pyfxr.chord() needs a positional root and rejected 'C4' in my test. pluck/tone give real musical note synthesis, so pyfxr covers build-time *music* material too, not just SFX.

3) KilledByAPixel/ZzFX (MIT). WORKING HEADLESS with a ~10-line shim. ZzFXMicro.js does `new AudioContext` at module load and ends by playing through Web Audio, so in Node you stub AudioContext and capture the buffer in createBuffer().getChannelData().set(). I did exactly that and wrote 4 WAVs (coin/laser/explosion/powerup). ZzFX's 20-parameter synth is a much wider design space than sfxr presets, and the whole DSP core is ~100 lines of plain math — it is the easiest of all of these to port straight to GDScript for *runtime* generation.

4) ttencate/jfxr (BSD-3-Clause, per-package LICENSE in lib/ and app/; root has none). Its Synth did compute a Clip in one of my attempts, but the API is callback-based (synth.doneCallback) and undocumented for Node, and I could not get a clean repeatable invocation. Marked honest: clonable and correctly licensed, headless usable only behind a wrapper someone has to write.

MUSIC — be honest: genuinely free music with a real licence is scarce, and much worse-verified than SFX.
- The one large corpus on GitHub, SoundSafari/CC0-1.0-Music (~9,292 files, ~40 GB, repo LICENSE is CC0), is aggregated by *source site*: freemusicarchive.org (5,181 files), freesound.org (2,998), chosic.com (798), freepd.com (302), pixbay.com (11). Only the freepd.com folder is from a source that is uniformly CC0. FMA and Chosic host large amounts of CC-BY, CC-BY-SA and NC material, so the blanket repo-level CC0 claim is NOT trustworthy for those folders. Recommend sparse-checkout of freepd.com only, and per-track verification for anything else.
- goblinhack/deceased-superior-technician-music is a LICENCE TRAP: the repo carries a CC0 LICENSE file, but its own README says the music was released "under a creative commons attribution license (just post a link to nosoapradio.us)". The mirror maintainer had no right to relicense to CC0. Treat as CC-BY with mandatory attribution, not CC0. Do not vendor on the strength of that LICENSE file.
- Kenney's Music Jingles (86 files, CC0) is the only music that is both properly licensed and small, and it is jingles/stingers, not tracks.
- Practical conclusion: for actual soundtrack music, plan on generating it (ZzFXM song format, pyfxr pluck/tone) or commissioning it, not on finding it.

BIGGEST ASSET WIN: lavenderdotpet/CC0-Public-Domain-Sounds turned out to mirror NINE Kenney CC0 audio packs on GitHub (kenney_uiaudio, kenney_interfacesounds, kenney_impactsounds, kenney_rpgaudio, kenney_digitalaudio, kenney_casinoaudio, kenney_musicjingles, kenney_voiceoverpack, kenney_voiceoverfighter) — each with its own License.txt, verified CC0, "Credit ... is not mandatory". kenney.nl itself is blocked in this sandbox, so this mirror is the only way to get those packs here. The full repo is 2,595 MB; a curated sparse-checkout of 22 paths is 58 MB / 1,410 audio files. Sparse checkout is mandatory here — do not clone it whole.

ATTRIBUTION SUMMARY: every asset pack I recommend vendoring is CC0 with attribution OPTIONAL (Kenney: "not mandatory"; Ben Burnes/Abstraction BB packs: "encouraged, but not required"; Warfork: Team Forbidden waived all rights; tidalcycles TR-808; subsoap chip-sounds). So no attribution file is legally required for the vendored set — though crediting Kenney is good practice.

GODOT 4.7 AUDIO NOTES (godot-docs is already vendored in third_party/, so the reference text is on disk): the nodes that matter for an undecided team are AudioStreamInteractive (state-machine music with clip transitions), AudioStreamPlaylist (ordered/shuffled sequences), and AudioStreamPolyphonic (multiple concurrent voices from ONE player — this makes most hand-rolled "audio pooling" addons partially redundant in Godot 4, worth knowing before adopting one). AudioServer exposes bus manipulation at runtime plus get_output_latency() for rhythm games; the standard rhythm-timing trick is AudioStreamPlayer.get_playback_position() + AudioServer.get_time_since_last_mix() - AudioServer.get_output_latency(). Web export is the pitfall: browser autoplay policy blocks audio until a user gesture, latency is much worse than desktop, and Ogg Vorbis is the safe format (MP3 can introduce gaps that break seamless loops — prefer .ogg for any looping music).

REJECTED ON LICENCE (verified, do not use):
- JimLynchCodes/Game-Sound-Effects — clonable but NO licence file anywhere. No rights granted. Reject.
- Bryce-Dixon/Godot_QuickAudio (27 stars) — no licence file. Reject.
- abrasivetroop/adaptive-audio-player — no licence file. Reject.
- mbitsnbites/soundbox — README: "The SoundBox editor is licensed under the GNU General Public License version 3". GPL, forbidden. Only its player-small.js is zlib; the repo as a whole cannot be vendored.
- increpare/bfxr (the original) — readme points at Apache-2.0, which is allowed, but it is ActionScript/AIR and its own readme says it is superseded by bfxr2. Use bfxr2 (MIT) instead.

Note on parallel-sweep overlap: nathanhoad/godot_dialogue_manager and Godot-GameTemplate surfaced during searching but belong to other domains; I did not pursue them.

domain_notes.domain: G — Procedural generation, AI and simulation
domain_notes.notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. Every candidate below was probed with `git ls-remote --heads` and a real `curl` of its licence file (root LICENSE/LICENSE.txt/LICENSE.md/COPYING on main and master, plus per-addon licence files where the root only pointed at one). Sizes marked measured_size_mb come from an actual `git clone --depth 1 --no-tags` + `du -sm`, and all clones were deleted afterwards. Nothing was written into /home/user/GODOT-GAME.

REJECTED FOR LICENCE — do not let these back in:
- quwatz/Godot-4-Dungeon-Generator (67 stars, Godot 4, Delaunay+MST corridors, the single most-linked Godot 4 dungeon generator): NO LICENSE FILE on main. A public repo with no licence grants no rights. Rejected despite being the best technical fit for the Delaunay/MST bullet.
- jeronimo-schreyer/godot-marching-cubes ("Cubes on the March", CPU+GPU marching cubes): GPL-3.0 (fetched: "GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3, 29 June 2007"). Forbidden.
- llasram/godot-visibility-demo (tile visibility + shadowcast + fov_composite shader): no licence file.
- Revolutionary-Games/Thrive (large Godot simulation game, surfaced by topic search): GPL — not fetched in detail, excluded on sight.
FLAGGED, NOT REJECTED: AsPJT/DungeonTemplateLibrary is BSL-1.0, which is permissive and MIT-equivalent in practice but is NOT on our stated allowlist — it needs a human sign-off before any derived code lands.

DELAUNAY/MST CORRIDORS — where it actually lives now that quwatz is out: gdquest-demos/godot-4-procedural-generation carries an MSTDungeon demo under godot3/ (MIT code, CC-BY art), and Godot ships Geometry2D.triangulate_delaunay() plus AStar2D in-engine, so the missing piece is only the MST pass over the triangulation. Treat the GDQuest godot3/MSTDungeon source as the reference and port it; that is a ~200-line job, not a dependency.

HONEST VERDICT ON ECS IN GODOT. Asked directly: no, do not adopt ECS as the project default. Godot's node/scene tree already is the composition mechanism, and every GDScript ECS pays an interpreter tax on the query/iterate loop that cancels the cache-locality benefit ECS exists for — you get the ceremony without the payoff. Editor tooling (inspector, scene instancing, animation, signals) is built around nodes, so an ECS layer means either duplicating that tooling or living outside it. GECS (CC0, already on Godot 4.7) is the best-designed compromise because Entities are Nodes and Components are Resources, so the editor still works; godothub/godot-ecs (MIT) is a lighter pure-GDScript take. The only case where ECS genuinely earns its place is tens of thousands of homogeneous entities updated every tick — and in Godot the better answers there are MultiMesh for rendering (see Proton Scatter), a C++/Rust GDExtension for the hot loop (see sand-slide, godot_boids), or godot-bevy/Klotho if the team is willing to leave GDScript entirely. Recommendation for an undecided team: skip ECS, revisit only if a chosen concept is provably entity-bound.

PATHFINDING — WHAT GODOT ALREADY GIVES US, so we do not vendor duplicates: AStar2D/AStar3D and AStarGrid2D are built in; NavigationServer2D/3D does navmesh pathfinding with baked regions, navigation links for jumps/teleports, and RVO2-based local avoidance via NavigationAgent (avoidance_enabled, radius, max_neighbors) — so "crowd avoidance" is a built-in, not a missing addon. What is genuinely missing and therefore worth an addon: flow fields for many-agents-one-goal (D2klaas Vector Field Navigation, arnemileswinter tilemap-flowfields), platformer jump-graph navigation (Surfacer), and hierarchical pathfinding, for which I found NO permissively-licensed Godot 4 implementation at all — that is a real gap to build if a large-map strategy game is chosen. NavigationServer best practice at scale is documented on docs.godotengine.org, which is blocked here (see unreachable list).

AI COVERAGE VS THE ALREADY-VENDORED beehave: beehave gives behaviour trees. The three complementary axes are covered above — GOAP (viniciusgerevini/godot-goap, plus aoiazure and RodZill4 variants, all verified MIT) for goal-directed planning, utility AI (Pennycook, plus viniciusgerevini, both MIT) for scored competing desires, and steering/flocking (konbel steering behaviors, 90-008/godot_boids) for the movement layer underneath all of them. Sensory systems (vision cones, hearing, memory) have no standalone permissive Godot 4 addon I could verify — in practice teams build them from Area2D/3D + raycast + the FOV code in the roguelike entries, which is why I indexed FOV separately.

RNG SEEDING AND REPRODUCIBILITY: no addon needed and none worth vendoring. Godot's RandomNumberGenerator exposes `seed` and `state`, so a reproducible run is (a) one RNG instance per subsystem, never the global randi(), (b) seed stored in the save, (c) state snapshotted alongside. The disciplined worked examples are snopek's godot-rollback-netcode (state serialisation + hashing per tick) and Klotho (seeded Xorshift128+ as an explicit determinism requirement). Note that Godot's built-in RNG is PCG32 and is NOT guaranteed identical across engine versions — for cross-version replay you must vendor your own PRNG.

EROSION: I could not find any permissively-licensed Godot 4 hydraulic/thermal erosion implementation on a reachable host. The known Godot erosion work (atif85's compute-shader erosion simulator) is itch.io-only and therefore unreachable and unvendorable. The transferable references are Unity/CUDA projects (bshishov/UnityTerrainErosionGPU, simonmeister/hydraulic-terrain-modeler) whose shader maths ports to Godot compute shaders. Treat erosion as "port from another engine", not "install an addon".

VENDORING SHORTLIST if you only take five: Gaea (procgen framework, already on 4.7), godot-constraint-solving/addons/wfc (WFC 2D+3D), gdquest-demos/godot-4-procedural-generation (algorithm catalogue, MIT code — record the CC-BY art attribution), SelinaDev roguelike part_12 + part_4 (FOV, turn scheduling), and godot-rollback-netcode (determinism, tick decoupling, replay). Two carry attribution obligations to record at vendor time: GDQuest art is CC-BY-4.0 ("GDQuest and contributors, https://www.gdquest.com/"), and Proton Scatter's GitHub copy is a mirror of a blocked Codeberg primary.

SCOPE NOTE: third_party/godot-docs is ALREADY vendored and already contains the authoritative pages for two big chunks of this domain — tutorials/i18n/{internationalizing_games,locales,localization_using_gettext,localization_using_spreadsheets,pseudolocalization}.rst and tutorials/export/{exporting_for_web,exporting_for_android,exporting_for_ios,exporting_for_macos,exporting_for_windows,android_gradle_build,feature_tags,one-click_deploy,running_on_macos}.rst. Route agents there FIRST; the repos below are the tooling layer on top.

ACCESSIBILITY — CURRENT TRUTH FOR 4.5/4.6/4.7 (this is the single most important correction to make in our notes):
* Screen readers are now BUILT IN. Godot 4.5 (Sept 2025) shipped a full AccessKit (https://github.com/accesskit/accesskit, Apache-2.0/MIT) integration. Control nodes expose an accessibility tree to NVDA/JAWS/Narrator/VoiceOver/Orca automatically, and there are per-Node bindings so you can describe non-Control nodes. Marked experimental; editor coverage is only Project Manager + inspector + standard UI nodes. Enable/disable via the `accessibility/general/accessibility_support` project setting (auto/always/disabled). DO NOT vendor the old Godot-3-era `lightsoutgames/godot-accessibility` screen-reader addon as a solution — it is superseded.
* TTS is also built in and has been since 4.x: `DisplayServer.tts_get_voices()`, `tts_speak()`, `tts_stop()`, `tts_is_speaking()`. On Linux it needs speech-dispatcher installed. The old `lightsoutgames/godot-tts` GDNative addon is superseded.
* Scalable UI/text: use `display/window/stretch/mode = canvas_items` + `scale` for global zoom, and a Theme with a `default_font_size` you multiply by a user "UI scale" setting; `Control.theme_override_font_sizes` on a per-node basis fights that, so avoid overrides in shipped UI. `RichTextLabel` respects theme font sizes; label auto-wrap must be on or scaled text clips.
* Colour-blind safety: never encode state in hue alone — pair hue with shape/icon/pattern/text. Safe default categorical palette is Okabe–Ito (8 colours, CVD-safe): #000000, #E69F00, #56B4E9, #009E73, #F0E442, #0072B2, #D55E00, #CC79A7. For sequential/diverging ramps use ColorBrewer schemes (ships inside d3-scale-chromatic, ISC). Ship a simulator (paulloz/godot-colorblindness) so designers can check, and a *correction* filter as a player option is a separate feature from simulation.
* Photosensitivity / reduced motion: cap full-screen luminance flashes to <3 per second, avoid >25% screen area of saturated red flashing, and expose a "reduce motion" toggle that disables screen shake, parallax, particle bursts and UI transitions (route all of these through one autoload multiplier so the toggle is a single value). The industry checker (PEAT, Trace Center) is Windows-only and not open source.
* Subtitles/captions: HauntedBees/Godot-Accessibility-Suite has an `.srt` importer + `CaptionedAudioStreamPlayer`; the accessible defaults are >=22px at 1080p, high-contrast background box behind text, speaker labels, and non-speech sound captions.
* Remappable controls: G.U.I.D.E or nathanhoad/godot_input_helper — do not hand-roll `InputMap.action_erase_events`/`action_add_event` persistence, both addons already serialise remaps.
* The canonical requirements checklist everyone implements against is gameaccessibilityguidelines.com (Basic/Intermediate/Advanced tiers).

INPUT:
* `Input.get_connected_joypads()` + the `joy_connection_changed` signal give hot-swap; "last device used" must be derived from the InputEvent type in `_input`, not from connection state (a plugged-in pad while the player types on a keyboard must show keyboard glyphs).
* Glyph packs: Xelu prompts and Kenney Input Prompts are both CC0, both mirrored on GitHub (see candidates), so redistribution inside our repo is legal.
* Haptics: `Input.start_joy_vibration(device, weak, strong, duration)` for gamepads, `Input.vibrate_handheld(ms)` for Android/iOS (iOS ignores the duration argument). Always gate behind a 0–100% intensity setting.
* Touch: `emulate_mouse_from_touch` is on by default and will silently make touch "work" badly; for real mobile UX use TouchScreenButton or a virtual joystick addon and set `Project Settings > Display > Window > Handheld > Orientation`.
* Safe areas (notched phones): `DisplayServer.get_display_safe_area()` returns a Rect2i in screen pixels — inset your root MarginContainer by it; there is no automatic handling.

LOCALISATION:
* Godot natively imports CSV (one column per locale, `keys,en,fr,...`, first column = message key) and gettext `.po`/`.pot`. CSV is easier for a small team, PO is what professional translators/Poedit expect — `Wiechciu/csv-to-gettext-converter` bridges the two.
* Built-in extraction exists: `Project > Tools > Localization > POT Generation` gathers strings from scenes/scripts, driven by `internationalization/locale/translation_add_builtin_strings_to_pot`.
* Pseudolocalization (`internationalization/pseudolocalization/*`) is the cheapest early win — turn it on to catch hard-coded strings and layouts that break at +40% string length before you pay a translator.
* RTL (Arabic/Hebrew) works out of the box only with the **TextServerAdvanced** module (default in official builds, but stripped in some custom/minimal builds); check before promising RTL. `Control.layout_direction` must be set to INHERITED/LOCALE for mirrored layouts, and mirroring of art/icons is manual.
* Fonts: Godot's default font has no CJK. Ship Noto Sans CJK or Sarasa Gothic (both OFL) and subset with fonttools (`pyftsubset`) — a full CJK OTF is 15–40MB, subsetting to the actual translated glyph set typically cuts it 90%+. OFL requires the licence be distributed with the font and forbids selling the font alone; it does NOT restrict the game.
* Attribution burden: CC0 needs none, OFL needs the licence file shipped, CC-BY needs a credits entry — keep one `CREDITS.md`/in-game credits screen generated from a machine-readable list.

PLATFORM / SHIPPING:
* Export templates must match the engine build exactly (4.7.x template for a 4.7.x editor); CI images (abarichello/godot-ci) exist precisely so this is pinned.
* Web export: threaded builds need cross-origin isolation — `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` + `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp`. itch.io has a "SharedArrayBuffer support" embed checkbox that uses `credentialless`, which Firefox and Firefox-for-Android historically do not implement, so a threaded build on itch is effectively Chromium-only. Two escapes: (a) untick "Thread Support" in the web export preset (single-threaded build, works everywhere, costs perf), or (b) coi-serviceworker, which fakes isolation from a service worker when you cannot set headers. Also serve `.wasm`/`.pck` with correct MIME types and gzip/brotli, and never host from `file://`.
* Web saves: `user://` is an Emscripten IDBFS mount backed by IndexedDB. Writes are NOT durable until synced — check `OS.is_userfs_persistent()`, and know that data is lost in private-browsing mode, when the browser evicts storage, and per-origin (a different itch.io game page is a different origin). Flush on `NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST`/`NOTIFICATION_APPLICATION_PAUSED`, not only on quit.
* Save locations elsewhere: Windows `%APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\<name>` (or `%APPDATA%\<name>` with `application/config/use_custom_user_dir`), macOS `~/Library/Application Support/Godot/app_userdata/<name>`, Linux `~/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/<name>`, Android/iOS app-sandbox. Steam Cloud needs an absolute path — resolve with `ProjectSettings.globalize_path("user://")`.
* Code signing: Windows Authenticode (EV/OV cert, otherwise SmartScreen warns), macOS requires Developer ID signing + notarisation + stapling or Gatekeeper blocks it — `rcodesign` from indygreg/apple-platform-rs does all of that from Linux/CI without a Mac. Android needs a release keystore; `debug` keystore builds cannot be updated later on Play.
* itch.io publishing = `butler push build/web user/game:html5 --userversion x.y.z`; butler does block-level diffing so pushes are cheap. Use the MIT `KikimoraGames/itch-publish` action, NOT `yeslayla/butler-publish-itchio-action` (GPL-3.0 — forbidden by our policy).
* Steam reality check: $100 recoupable fee per app, 2-week mandatory review + 2-week store-page-visible-before-release rule, build must run without the SDK present (`SteamAPI_Init` failure must degrade gracefully). Console (Switch/PS/Xbox) has no open-source path for Godot — it requires a licensed porting partner (W4 Games, Pineapple Works, Lone Wolf) under NDA; do not plan console in-house.
* Telemetry/crash: getsentry/sentry-godot is the only first-party-quality crash reporter (MIT, needs Godot 4.5+, web supported since 1.4.0). For gameplay analytics, self-hosted Umami (MIT) keeps data on our infra; avoid Plausible/Matomo/Countly for vendoring (AGPL/GPL). Privacy-respecting means: no device fingerprinting, opt-in on first run, a stable random install-id (not IDFA/GAID), event names only, and a documented deletion path.

LICENCE TRAPS FOUND IN THIS SWEEP (record these):
* `yeslayla/butler-publish-itchio-action` is GPL-3.0 — rejected.
* `CoaguCo-Industries/GodotSteam` on GitHub is now an empty pointer repo (README only, no LICENCE); the real MIT project moved to Codeberg, which is blocked here.
* `axismaps/colorbrewer` and `Zylann/godot_translation_editor` have NO LICENSE file in-repo — rejected under our no-licence rule (use d3-scale-chromatic for the ColorBrewer data instead, and the MIT localisation editors instead of Zylann's).
* `ETdoFresh/kenney.nl` has no root LICENSE, but every asset pack folder carries Kenney's own CC0 `license.txt` — vendor per-folder only, and vendor the licence file with it.
* `rsubtil/controller_icons`: MIT code + CC0 Xelu art, but the addon's own icon derives from the Godot logo (CC-BY-4.0) — either drop that one file or record the attribution.
* `tolgee/tolgee-platform` is Apache-2.0 except `ee/` and `webapp/src/ee` which are proprietary-EE — usable only if we exclude those trees.
* `indygreg/apple-platform-rs` is MPL-2.0 (flagged, allowed) — file-level copyleft, fine for a CLI we invoke.

domain_notes.domain: Gameplay addons and subsystems (permissive, Godot 4.x, desktop/Steam)
domain_notes.notes:
METHOD. Fetched raw.githubusercontent.com/godotengine/awesome-godot/master/README.md (511 lines) and read the Plugins-and-scripts (lines 200-376), Projects (118-137), Templates (138-164) and Demos (165-193) sections in full, then supplemented with GitHub repository search for the categories awesome-godot covers thinly (object pooling, save systems, localisation, tooltips, damage numbers, performance overlays). Every candidate below was verified with `git ls-remote --heads` plus a real `curl` of the licence file, and every vendor/vendor-sparse candidate was sized with `git clone --depth 1 --no-tags` + `du -sm`, then deleted. Nothing was written into /home/user/GODOT-GAME.

VERDICT — OBJECT POOLING: HAND-ROLL IT. This was an explicit ask and the honest answer is that no addon is worth the dependency. The entire GitHub field is: godot-addons/godot-object-pool (49 stars, MIT verified, but written in 2016 for Godot 2/3 and unmaintained), NovemberDev/novemberdev_object_pooling_godot (22 stars), sempitern0/Fast-Pool (14 stars, MIT verified, 2025, the best of the lot), and roughly fifteen sub-10-star C# repos. Compare with the state-machine field, where derkork/godot-statecharts and LimboAI both have thousands of users. That asymmetry is not an accident: a pool is 80-150 lines, and the hard part is not the pool container, it is the per-type reset contract (what does a bullet clear when it is released? what does an enemy clear?). An addon cannot supply that, so it saves almost nothing while adding an update burden. Concretely, hand-roll a Pool node that (a) pre-instantiates N copies of a PackedScene at load, (b) keeps free instances out of the active tree via remove_child rather than free(), (c) calls a `_on_pooled_reset()` convention on acquire, and (d) grows by a configurable increment when exhausted. Also note that pooling matters far less in Godot 4 than in Unity — Godot has no GC to spike, RefCounted is deterministic, and the real cost is scene instantiation, not allocation. Profile before pooling anything; if you need a reference implementation, read sempitern0/Fast-Pool.

VERDICT — SAVE/LOAD AND VERSIONED MIGRATION: BUILD IT, WITH TWO VENDORED COMPONENTS. There is no good general Godot 4 save addon. The GitHub field (searched topic:godot topic:save-system) is all sub-25-star projects, several of which are freemium lures with the real features behind an itch.io paywall (youssof20/savestate advertises exactly this) — those are policy-hostile regardless of the stated MIT licence on the Lite tier. What we should vendor instead are the two pieces that are genuinely hard to get right: derkork/godot-safe-resource-loader, because saving custom Resources is the ergonomic Godot idiom and loading an untrusted .tres executes embedded GDScript (a real RCE hole in any game with cloud saves, mods, or Workshop content); and, if we pick a simulation-shaped genre, 2shady4u/godot-sqlite for incremental transactional writes over a large world. For the migration layer specifically, no addon exists at any quality level — write a plain `version: int` field plus an ordered list of migration functions applied in sequence, and pin the schema version into the save at write time. Read TinyTakinTeller/TakinGodotTemplate for a worked multi-slot save integration and Maaack's Godot-Game-Template (already vendored) for the settings-persistence half.

VERDICT — LOCALISATION WORKFLOW: GODOT'S BUILT-IN PIPELINE IS THE ANSWER; THE GAP IS AUTHORING ERGONOMICS. Godot 4 already ships CSV and gettext/PO import, automatic POT generation from scenes and scripts, per-locale font fallbacks, TranslationServer, and pseudolocalisation for layout testing — that is a stronger built-in story than most engines and none of the addons in awesome-godot improve on it. The two genuine gaps are (1) comfortably editing a large string table, which don-tnowe/godot-resources-as-sheets-plugin solves with a spreadsheet grid and CSV round-trip, and (2) strings containing runtime variables and live locale switching, which phosxd/PowerKey targets. dannygaray60/localization-editor-g3 (36 stars) is Godot 3 and fenix-hub/godot-engine.file-editor is a general file editor with CSV translation support — both are weaker than just using the spreadsheet plugin. Recommendation: built-in POT/CSV pipeline + resources_spreadsheet_view for authoring, and revisit PowerKey only if dynamic strings become painful.

VERDICT — NUMBER FORMATTING, TOOLTIPS, EASING: HAND-ROLL OR USE BUILT-INS, NOTHING TO VENDOR. Number formatting (thousands separators, abbreviated 1.2M/3.4B for incremental games, percentage and duration formatting) has no credible Godot addon and is genuinely twenty lines of String manipulation — write it, and make it locale-aware via TranslationServer if we localise. Tooltips: Control.tooltip_text plus an overridden `_make_custom_tooltip()` covers rich tooltips natively; a GitHub search for Godot 4 tooltip addons returned exactly one zero-star result, which tells you the built-in is adequate. Easing: Godot 4's Tween has the full Robert Penner set via Tween.TransitionType/EaseType, plus Curve resources for arbitrary shapes and `@GlobalScope.ease()`/`lerp_angle()` helpers — impmja/godot-easing in awesome-godot is a Godot 2-era port that adds nothing. Damage numbers and floating combat text likewise have no maintained addon worth the dependency (the only search hit was a 3-star repo); build it as a pooled Label3D/Label with a Tween, using our own pool.

VERDICT — DIALOGIC GAP ANALYSIS (explicitly requested). Dialogic ships inside godot-open-rpg and is a strong visual timeline/graph authoring tool with a batteries-included presentation layer — dialogue boxes, character portraits, expressions, backgrounds, typing effects, choice buttons, and a variable/condition system. What it does NOT do well: (a) its .dtl timeline files are effectively binary-ish to git, so two writers editing the same conversation is a merge conflict, which matters for any team of more than one; (b) it is opinionated about presentation — bending it into an existing custom HUD is fighting it; (c) it is heavy for one-line barks and environmental text, where the ceremony of a timeline is pure overhead; (d) it does not model quests, only conditions; (e) engineer-driven dialogue (dialogue generated or selected in code) is awkward. nathanhoad/godot_dialogue_manager is the precise complement on every one of those axes — plain-text source that merges in git, no bundled UI, trivial one-liners, direct callbacks into game autoloads, and CSV/PO translation export. Recommendation: vendor Dialogue Manager alongside Dialogic and let the genre decide (visual-novel-shaped → Dialogic; RPG/immersive-sim/action with scattered text → Dialogue Manager). For quests, which neither tool covers, vendor Questify (graph-authored) with QuestSystem indexed as the code-authored alternative. Other alternatives considered and rejected for our purposes: godot-ink (C#/Mono only — wrong runtime for a GDScript project, and it drags in the ink dependency), Konado and Sprouty Dialogs (both narrower re-treads of Dialogic with far less adoption), Orchestrator (visual scripting first, dialogue second — a much larger commitment), Rubonnek/dialogue-engine (minimal, but so minimal it is not worth a dependency).

REJECTED ON LICENCE (recorded so nobody re-proposes them). Rubonnek/inventory-manager — public repo with NO licence file anywhere: checked master/LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt, COPYING, addons/*/LICENSE and the README, all absent or 404. Under our policy that grants zero rights, so it is forbidden despite being a reasonable-looking minimal inventory addon; use peter-kish/gloot instead. Two licence traps worth recording for the index: bitwes/Gut has NO root LICENSE (it is at addons/gut/LICENSE.md, MIT) so a root-only audit would wrongly reject it, and DmitriySalnikov/godot_debug_draw_3d's root LICENSE is a one-line pointer to addons/debug_draw_3d/LICENSE (MIT) so a naive fetch reads as garbage. glass-brick/Scene-Manager has no LICENSE on its default `main` branch — the MIT file only exists on the `godot-4.x` branch, which is the branch we want anyway.

CATEGORY COVERAGE AFTER THIS SWEEP. FSM/HSM: godot-statecharts (vendor) + beehave already vendored + LimboAI indexed as the escalation path. Pooling: hand-roll, Fast-Pool indexed. Save/persistence: safe-resource-loader (vendor) + godot-sqlite (indexed, genre-contingent) + Takin template as reference; migration is ours to write. Settings/input/glyphs: Input Helper + Controller Icons (both vendor) on top of Maaack's options menus, which is a complete Steam Deck story. Juice: Juicee + Shaker (vendor) on top of phantom-camera. UI: ThemeGen + Kenyoni's aspect_ratio_resize_container and custom_theme_overrides (vendor); tooltips and number formatting are built-in/hand-rolled. Localisation: built-in + resources_spreadsheet_view (vendor). Debug: Panku Console + Godot Debug Menu + Signal Lens + Debug Draw 3D + Godot Doctor (all vendor) — five orthogonal views, the strongest cluster in this sweep. Scene flow: Scene Manager (vendor) + Maaack's loader. Inventory/dialogue/quests: GLoot + Pandora + Dialogue Manager + Questify (vendor). Compliance: Kenyoni `licenses` addon (vendor) — needed because this repo is itself a pile of third-party licences that must be surfaced in-game before we ship.

DELIBERATE NON-OVERLAP WITH THE PARALLEL SWEEP. Excluded as belonging to the parallel sweep's territory: netcode (netfox, foxssake tooling), procedural generation (ProtonScatter, Dungeon Template Library), 2D/3D art pipeline (Aseprite Wizard, Importality, AnimSheet, AntialiasedLine2D, SmartShape2D, func_godot, Cyclops Level Builder, YATI/Tiled), audio middleware and asset tooling (FMOD, Wwise, Event Audio, Godot Mixing Desk), accessibility/platform (GATO toolkit, Steam integration), and genre kits/templates (COGITO, First Person Starter, Godot XR Template). Also excluded as already vendored or bundled: Beehave, Dialogic, Maaack's Game Template and its Menus/Scene-Loader components, Phantom Camera, Terrain3D, gdUnit4, godot-demo-projects.

domain_notes.domain: Complete open-source Godot 4 games worth studying (shipped and substantially complete), across genres
domain_notes.notes:
METHOD. Mined the full Games section of awesome-godot (raw master README, 511 lines) — its Godot 4 lists are thin (5 entries under 2D, 9 under 3D) and roughly half sit on codeberg.org, which is unreachable here. Went well beyond it with GitHub repository search (topic:godot / godot4 / godot-game, plus top GDScript repos by stars pushed since Sept 2025) and, most productively, GitHub CODE search for `"godotsteam" filename:project.godot`, which surfaces games that actually integrated Steamworks — that query is how Dot Hop, Fortune Mill and Alchemia were found and is worth re-running periodically. Every candidate was verified with `git ls-remote --heads` plus a raw.githubusercontent.com fetch of LICENSE / LICENSE.txt / LICENSE.md / LICENCE / COPYING across main and master; the identifying line is quoted in license_evidence for all 29 entries. Engine version was read from each repo's real project.godot (config_version and config/features), not from README claims — this caught Tabletop Club and Turbo Fat as Godot 3 (config_version=4) despite both being active in 2026. Sizes came from real `git clone --depth 1 --no-tags` + `du -sm`, then the clones were deleted; nothing was written into /home/user/GODOT-GAME.

CONFIRMED STEAM RELEASES from a Godot 4 codebase we can legally read: Dot Hop (app 2779710), Tanks of Freedom II (3071660), A Dark Forest (3314970), Bread Adventure (3835290), Fortune Mill (4731620, released 2 June 2026), Museum of All Things, plus Pixelorama and Material Maker as shipped Godot 4.7 apps, and Thrive (GPL, link-only). That is the core of the "last 20%" evidence: achievements, multi-slot saves, retrofitted localisation, settings/keybinds, platform abstraction and release CI all appear in these repos and almost nowhere else.

LICENCE REALITY. The split-licence trap is the norm, not the exception, in game repos: five of the strongest candidates grant MIT to code only. Dot Hop and dino say so in the LICENSE file itself ("Source code and documentation only!"); YouTD 2 puts CC-BY-NC on all assets (forbidden — vendor src/ only); A Dark Forest mixes CC0, CC-BY, CC-BY-SA and CC-BY-NC-SA across shaders/music; Tanks of Freedom II is MIT for code and graphics but CC-BY-SA for its audio and proprietary for docs/. The sparse_paths in this report are chosen specifically to keep forbidden assets out of third_party/ — following them is mandatory, not advisory. Bread Adventure, godot-open-rts, OpenCiv3, OpenVic, OpenLiberty, Escoria and Pixelorama are the clean full-tree vendors. Two entries are logged as explicit negative results (a-little-game-called-mario's Anti-Capitalist licence; SMB Remastered's GPL + Nintendo IP) so they are not re-proposed, and three otherwise-recommended repos (Arrow, ROTA, starship-olympics) were probed and have NO licence file at all — recorded under unreachable_but_worth_indexing.

GENRE COVERAGE ACHIEVED (for routing "we picked genre X"): puzzle → Dot Hop; turn-based strategy → Tanks of Freedom II; RTS → godot-open-rts; 4X/grand strategy → OpenCiv3, OpenVic; tower defense → YouTD 2; incremental/idle → Fortune Mill, A Dark Forest; metroidvania/2D platformer → Bread Adventure, dino, moddable-platformer; tactics RPG → godot-tactical-rpg; first-person exploration/procedural 3D → Museum of All Things; open world → OpenLiberty; point-and-click adventure → Escoria; god/agent sim → Microverse; party/minigame → Super Tux Party (link-only); deckbuilder → Alchemia (link-only, Godot 3); city builder → Unknown Horizons (link-only); rhythm → Rhythia (link-only). GENUINE GAPS, permissively licensed and Godot 4: FPS/shooter and horror — the only credible open ones (Sunder, LibreAim) are codeberg-hosted and unreachable; racing/driving; and survivors-likes, where nothing open and complete was found.

NON-DUPLICATION. Deliberately excluded as the parallel sweep's territory: godot-tiny-mmo and jdungeon (netcode), Zylann/voxelgame and the gdquest procedural-generation demos (procgen), godot-shaders and stylized-sky (art/shaders), Maaack / crystal-bit / TakinGodotTemplate (templates, and Maaack is already vendored), and pure addons (Metroidvania-System, pandora, gloot, netfox, comedot). Pixelorama is included despite being an application, tagged as such, because it is the most complete legally-readable example of Godot 4.7 release engineering; Material Maker, GodSVG and Lorien were licence-verified as MIT siblings and folded into its notes rather than given separate entries.

domain_notes.domain: Training and learning material that can live in the repo as text (Godot 4.7, desktop/Steam, genre-undecided)
domain_notes.notes:
Method: every candidate was probed with `git ls-remote --heads` and a raw.githubusercontent.com fetch of LICENSE / LICENSE.md / LICENSE.txt / COPYING on the real default branch; sizes come from `git clone --depth 1 --no-tags` + `du -sk` (all clones deleted). api.github.com is blocked for raw curl but the github MCP `search_repositories` tool worked, which is how the gdquest-demos org (53 repos) and PacktPublishing's Godot catalogue were enumerated — `get_file_contents` is NOT available (session is scoped to ats314/godot-game only), so all content inspection was done by cloning.

Key findings that shape the recommendations:

1. GDQuest dual-licence trap. Almost every gdquest-demos repo ships a LICENSE that reads "This project uses 2 licenses: 1. The demo's source code ... MIT. 2. Art assets (image textures and 3D models) are CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0." CC-BY-NC-SA is on our FORBIDDEN list. The MIT code is fine; the art is not. So the correct action for godot-design-patterns and godot-4-how-tos is vendor-sparse (code directories only), never a full clone. Two GDQuest repos are the exception and use CC-BY 4.0 for art (godot-mini-tuts-demos, learn-gdscript) — but both are Godot 3 projects (project.godot has `config_version=4`; Godot 4 uses 5), so they fail on relevance instead.

2. The single best "patterns in GDScript" repo is unlicensed. PacktPublishing/Game-Development-Patterns-with-Godot-4 (221 stars, 13 chapters: composition, singleton, observer, factory, state, command, strategy, decorator, service locator, event queue — exactly our shopping list) has NO LICENSE file anywhere: LICENSE/LICENSE.md/LICENSE.txt/COPYING all 404 on `main`, the cloned root contains only .gitignore/README.md/chapter dirs, and the README contains no licence text. Under our policy that grants zero rights. Same for Godot-4-Game-Development-Projects-Second-Edition. Both are link-only. The gap is filled by PacktPublishing/Godot-4-Best-Practices, which IS MIT and IS Godot 4.6 Forward+.

3. Game Programming Patterns (Nystrom) cannot be vendored. Its LICENSE explicitly splits: '.markdown', '.html', '.txt' files are CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; only '.py'/'.h'/'.cpp' are MIT. The prose — the part we actually want — is NoDerivatives + NonCommercial. This is the clearest DISTILL case in the domain: the ideas are not copyrightable, so we write our own GDScript-flavoured condensation and cite the book.

4. Steam is the thinnest area. GodotSteam and GodotSteam-Docs still exist on GitHub but both repos' master branch now contains a single readme.md saying "This repository has been moved to Codeberg" — and codeberg.org is blocked. Neither GitHub remnant has a LICENSE file. The only verified-permissive written Steam material I found is inside jame581/GodotPrompter (skills/export-pipeline/references/distribution-itch-steam.md + ci-cd-github-actions.md, MIT) and aBARICHELLO/godot-ci (MIT, headless export automation). Steam-specific knowledge beyond that should be DISTILLED by us from Valve's partner docs, which are all-rights-reserved and must never be pasted in.

5. The two agent-skill repos are the highest-value new find for this domain and neither duplicates anything already vendored. vl4dt/godot-skills (MIT, 21 SKILL.md files, 1.26 MB, explicitly declares godot-4.7 compatibility in each skill's front-matter and ships docs/migration-4.7.md) and jame581/GodotPrompter (MIT, 55 skills / 249 markdown files, 4.3 MB) are dense, greppable, already structured as "question → answer" units. Caveat worth recording in the index: godot-skills' 4.7 notes include at least one claim I could not corroborate ("Steam Frame configuration"), so treat both as strong starting points to be checked against the vendored 4.7 class reference, not as authority. A third similar repo, thedivergentai/GD-Agentic-Skills (488 stars), is LGPL-3.0 and is therefore rejected outright.

6. KidsCanCode Godot Recipes is vendorable and should be sparse. The repo is MIT (LICENSE: "MIT License / Copyright (c) 2019 KidsCanCode") with a CC-BY 4.0 badge alongside it in the README for the prose. A full clone is 747 MB because docs/ (370 MB) is the built site and static_shared/ (156 MB) is images. The Godot 4 recipe source is src-4/content: 117 markdown files, 800 KB, Hugo front-matter, categories ai/ ui/ basics/ physics/ 2D/ 3D/ input/ audio/ shaders/ animation/ math/ g101/. Sparse-checkout that one path and the whole thing costs less than a megabyte.

VENDORED vs DISTILLED, as a rule for this domain: vendor anything that is already structured prose or already-typed GDScript under a permissive licence (recipes, skills, architecture advice, Packt best-practices code, awesome-godot). Distil where the licence blocks us (Game Programming Patterns, Valve/Steamworks docs, godotrecipes.com's Godot 3 half) or where the material is scattered across the official manual we already have (static typing, signals, autoloads, node-vs-resource, performance — abmarnie's document plus the two skill repos already condense these better than we would; write our own only for the Steam shipping checklist).

Deliberately excluded as parallel-sweep territory: gdquest-demos genre kits (godot-2d-builder, godot-2d-tower-defense, godot-2d-jrpg-combat, godot-2d-tactical-rpg-movement, godot-platformer-2d, godot-4-3d-third-person-controller), godot-4-procedural-generation, godot-shaders, godot-visual-effects, godot-4-VFX-assets, godot-4-3D-Characters.

domain_notes.domain: Tooling, testing, CI and build infrastructure (Godot 4.7.1, desktop/Steam)
domain_notes.notes:
EVERYTHING BELOW WAS EXERCISED, NOT JUST READ. Godot 4.7.1 headless runs in this sandbox: `curl -sSL -o godot.zip https://github.com/godotengine/godot-builds/releases/download/4.7.1-stable/Godot_v4.7.1-stable_linux.x86_64.zip` returned HTTP 200 / 76,056,717 bytes in <1s and `./Godot_v4.7.1-stable_linux.x86_64 --headless --version` printed `4.7.1.stable.official.a13da4feb`. That means CI recipes here are verified, not guessed. The matching templates URL is .../4.7.1-stable/Godot_v4.7.1-stable_export_templates.tpz (tag 4.7.1-stable confirmed present in godotengine/godot-builds).

=== GDSCRIPT TOOLKIT: INSTALLED AND RUN ===
`pip install "gdtoolkit==4.*"` installed gdtoolkit 4.5.0 (PyPI reachable). Binaries: /usr/local/bin/{gdparse,gdlint,gdformat,gd2py,gdradon}. MIT (setup.py `license="MIT"`, LICENSE = "MIT License Copyright (c) 2019 Pawel Lampe").
4.7 SYNTAX SUPPORT — I bisected feature by feature with gdparse. ALL of these parse OK: typed Dictionary[String,int], `@abstract` on class AND on func, `match ... _ when cond:` guards, `@export_tool_button`, `@export_custom`, `static var`, typed lambdas, `&"StringName"` literals, `for i: int in ...`, typed signal params, inline get/set. The ONLY failure was `Dictionary[String, Array[int]]` — and Godot itself does not support nested typed containers, so that is not a real gap. Verdict: gdtoolkit 4.5.0 is fully usable on 4.7.1 GDScript.
gdlint config: `gdlint --dump-default-config` writes a `gdlintrc` (class-definitions-order, function-name regex incl. `_on_Signal_name`, function-arguments-number: 10, etc.) — edit and commit it.
`gdradon cc file.gd` gives per-function cyclomatic complexity (A/B/C grades) — free complexity gate.
gdformat emits TAB indentation, matching the Godot style guide, and left my hand-written file unchanged except for its own normalisation pass.

=== PRE-COMMIT: RUN END TO END ===
`pip install pre-commit` (4.6.1) then a .pre-commit-config.yaml pointing at Scony/godot-gdscript-toolkit. IMPORTANT PIN: `rev: 4.3.4` FAILED on `@abstract func` ("Unexpected token ... Expected COLON"). `rev: 4.5.0` PASSED gdlint and correctly reformatted with gdformat. Use rev 4.5.0 or newer. The repo ships .pre-commit-hooks.yaml with ids `gdlint` and `gdformat` (types: [gdscript]).

=== HEADLESS VALIDATION — WHAT ACTUALLY CATCHES BREAKAGE (all measured on a deliberately broken project) ===
1. `godot --headless --path . --import --quit-after 2` — builds .godot/, exit 0. It did NOT report the broken script or the missing texture. Import alone is NOT a validation gate.
2. `godot --headless --path . --check-only --script res://bad.gd` — THE reliable script gate. Real exit code 1 on a bad script, 0 on a good one, and it prints full analyzer errors ("Cannot assign a value of type String to variable "x" with specified type int", "Function "undefined_function_call()" not found in base self"). It does NOT accept a directory (`--script res://` errors), so loop over `find . -name '*.gd'`. Verified: loop flagged exactly bad.gd.
3. `godot --headless --path . --doctool OUT --gdscript-docs res://` — one-shot sweep over the whole project. Generated per-class XML (Documented.xml with brief_description/description/methods pulled from `##` comments) AND surfaced the parse errors for the broken script in stderr. Exit code is 0 regardless, so gate on `grep -cE '^(SCRIPT )?ERROR:'`. Doubles as free API-reference generation.
4. LOAD-EVERYTHING HARNESS — the important trap: I wrote a `@tool extends SceneTree` script walking res:// and calling ResourceLoader.load(..., CACHE_MODE_IGNORE) on every .tscn/.tres. Against a scene with `ext_resource path="res://missing.png"` and a bogus `uid://deadbeefdead1`, Godot printed `WARNING: ... invalid UID: uid://deadbeefdead1 - using text path instead`, `ERROR: Resource file not found: res://missing.png`, `ERROR: [ext_resource] referenced non-existent resource` — BUT load() STILL RETURNED A NON-NULL PackedScene and instantiate() succeeded, so my failure list was EMPTY and the script exited 0. CONCLUSION: never gate on return values; capture stderr and fail on `^(ERROR|SCRIPT ERROR|USER ERROR):`. This is the single most useful finding in this domain.
5. CRASH WARNING: including `.gd` files in that ResourceLoader walk SEGFAULTED Godot 4.7.1 (signal 11, reproducible) when it hit a script with parse errors. Exclude .gd from the resource walk; use --check-only for scripts. Also: SceneTree entry point must be `_initialize()`, not `_init()`.
Recommended gate = gdlint (fast, no engine) -> --import -> --check-only loop -> load-everything + stderr grep -> gdUnit4/GUT.

=== GUT vs gdUnit4 — BOTH ACTUALLY RUN ON 4.7.1 HEADLESS, HERE IS THE HONEST COMPARISON ===
GUT: use branch `godot_4_7` / tag v9.7.1 (main branch is 4.6.x only — the README version table is explicit). Command that worked: `godot --headless --path . -s addons/gut/gut_cmdln.gd -gdir=res://test -ginclude_subdirs -gexit`. Note `-ginclude_subdirs` is REQUIRED or you get "Nothing was run" with exit 0 — a silent green CI. Reported 2 tests / 1 failure and exited 1. Has `-gjunit_xml_file` for JUnit XML, `.gutconfig.json` for config, `-gexit_on_success`. Clone 13 MB.
gdUnit4: master = 6.2.1, README badges list v4.7 and v4.7.1 explicitly. Command that worked: `GODOT_BIN=... ./addons/gdUnit4/runtest.sh --headless --ignoreHeadlessMode --add res://test`. Two warts found live: (a) without `--ignoreHeadlessMode` it hard-refuses headless with exit 103 — a CI footgun; (b) runtest.sh does not add --headless itself, so without it you get X11/Wayland failures. Once past that: ran 2 tests, 1 failure, exit 100, and auto-wrote reports/report_1/results.xml (JUnit) AND index.html with zero config. Also tracks orphan nodes ("0 orphans") — genuinely valuable for leak detection in a game.
RECOMMENDATION: gdUnit4 for this repo. Reasons: (1) it is ALREADY vendored at 6.1.3 inside third_party/beehave/addons/gdUnit4, so adopting it costs nothing and avoids two competing frameworks in one project; (2) first-party GitHub Action (godot-gdunit-labs/gdUnit4-action, MIT) vs GUT having none; (3) XML+HTML reports and orphan-node tracking out of the box; (4) fluent assertions (assert_int(x).is_equal(y)) and scene/input simulation runners. GUT's advantages are real but narrower: much smaller (13 MB vs 66 MB), simpler mental model, better docs (gut.readthedocs.io), and its 4.7 branch is version-pinned so there is no ambiguity. If the team already knows GUT, GUT is fine — both are MIT and both work. Do NOT run both.

=== CI SHAPE THAT I WOULD ACTUALLY WRITE ===
Simplest and most controllable: no docker image at all. `actions/cache` (MIT) keyed on `godot-4.7.1-stable`, restoring ~/godot-bin and ~/.local/share/godot/export_templates/4.7.1.stable; on miss, curl the two godot-builds URLs above, unzip the .tpz and `mv templates/* ~/.local/share/godot/export_templates/4.7.1.stable/`. Then `godot --headless --path . --import --quit-after 2`, the validation gates, tests, then `godot --headless --path . --export-release "Windows Desktop" build/game.exe` and `--export-release "Linux/X11" build/game.x86_64`. Steam Deck ships from the Linux preset (x86_64, Forward+); no separate preset needed.
If you want a prepackaged path, abarichello/godot-ci (MIT) has a `4.7.1-stable` tag and an action.yml. TWO CAVEATS I VERIFIED: the Dockerfile in the 4.7.1-stable tree still has `ARG GODOT_VERSION="4.5"` as its default (stale), and action.yml references `docker://barichello/godot-ci` with NO TAG — always pin `barichello/godot-ci:4.7.1` explicitly in your workflow rather than trusting either default.
firebelley/godot-export (MIT) reads export_presets.cfg and exports every preset, with `cache: true` for engine+templates — the least-code option, but you feed it explicit download URLs.
chickensoft-games/setup-godot (MIT) installs Godot 4.x on ubuntu/windows/macos runners with caching and sets $GODOT — cleanest if you ever want to matrix across runner OSes.

=== STEAM ===
game-ci/steam-deploy@v3 (MIT) wraps steamcmd: `username` + `configVdf` secret (or password + TOTP via CyberAndrii/steam-totp, MIT), `appId`, `rootPath`, `depot1Path`/`depot2Path`, `depot1InstallScriptPath`, `releaseBranch`. Depot layout for us: depot1 = Windows export dir, depot2 = Linux export dir, releaseBranch=prerelease until you are ready. steamcmd itself and the Steamworks SDK are Valve proprietary — not vendorable, only invoked. GodotSteam (achievements/overlay/Steam Input) has MOVED OFF GITHUB TO CODEBERG (the GitHub repo now contains only a redirect readme and NO LICENSE file) — it is blocked from this sandbox; see unreachable list.

=== PROFILING ===
Godot 4.6+ integrates Tracy/Perfetto in the BUILD SYSTEM (`profiler_path=` scons arg), which means it requires compiling the engine from source — not usable with the stock 4.7.1 binary. For day-to-day work the practical tools are the built-in editor profiler/monitors, and godot-extended-libraries/godot-debug-menu (MIT, 1 MB): F3 cycles an id-Tech-style overlay with FPS, frametime, CPU time, GPU time graphs, best/worst/avg, and hardware/driver info, works in exported builds and on Forward+ — exactly right for Steam Deck perf bring-up. Vendor it.

=== .editorconfig FOR GDSCRIPT (from godotengine/godot's own .editorconfig, fetched) ===
root = true / [*] charset=utf-8, end_of_line=lf, indent_style=tab, indent_size=4, insert_final_newline=true, trim_trailing_whitespace=true, max_line_length=120; [*.{yml,yaml}] indent_style=space, indent_size=2. GDScript MUST be tabs — gdformat already emits tabs, so gdformat + this .editorconfig agree.

=== LSP / EDITOR ===
Godot's built-in LSP listens on 127.0.0.1:6005; godotengine/godot-vscode-plugin (MIT) is the reference client and also gives .tscn/.tres syntax and a debug adapter (port 6006). PrestonKnopp/tree-sitter-gdscript (MIT) is the grammar behind nvim/helix highlighting and is also the practical way for an agent to parse GDScript structurally outside the engine.

WHAT IS ALREADY VENDORED (assessed directly, read-only)

third_party/ShaderV (MIT, arkology, Godot 4.x, ~1211 stars upstream): a VisualShader NODE library, not a shader library. It supplies building blocks only: noise (Perlin/Simplex/Worley 2D/3D/4D plus fractal variants), blur (9-sample, custom N-sample, zoom), procedural shapes (circle, regular polygon, spiral, grid, checkerboard, sharp scanlines, random stripes), inner/outer glow, and colour ops (BCS, HSV shift, gradient map, posterize, greyscale, CGA-4 and Game Boy palettes, chromatic aberration, emboss, tonemap, shine). Every node is canvas_item/2D and only usable from the VisualShader graph editor — there is no .gdshader text you can copy, no spatial/3D node, and no finished effect.

library/code/shaders.tsv (55 shaders) breaks down as: Terrain3D 5 (terrain lightweight/minimum, ocean, grass particles + wind); godot-demo-projects 2d/screen_space_shaders 11 (BCS, blur, contrast, mirage, negative, normalized, old_film, pixelize, sepia, vignette, whirl); 2d/sprite_shaders 9 (aura, blur, dissintegrate, dropshadow, fatty, glow, offsetshadow, outline, silhouette); 3d/sprites paper/billboard 5; sky 2 (panorama skybox, sky_volumetric_clouds — this is clayjohn's volumetric cloud demo upstreamed, so that repo is redundant); misc 8 (plasma, gradient steps, hues, curvature, VRS, compute water_plane, HDR color sweep, noise viewer, split screen); XR 9 (irrelevant — desktop target); godot-open-rpg/Dialogic 4 (two background wipe/push transitions, two speech-bubble wobbles).

THE REMAINING GAP, CONCRETELY. Nothing vendored covers: (1) CompositorEffect — Godot 4's actual post-process API — zero examples exist in the repo; (2) 3D outline / toon / cel shading of any kind; (3) CRT, VHS, glitch, scanline or retro-console filters (old_film is the nearest thing); (4) a screen/scene transition shader library (Dialogic's two background wipes are the only transitions and they are locked inside Dialogic); (5) 3D water beyond Terrain3D's ocean plane — no SSR water, no FFT ocean, no 2D water at all; (6) sky beyond the one official volumetric-cloud demo — no atmospheric scattering, no time-of-day system, no stylised sky; (7) grass/foliage/wind beyond Terrain3D's single particle shader; (8) fire, smoke, explosions, lasers, beams or trails — completely absent; (9) dissolve, force-field/shield, status-effect (frozen/petrified/poisoned/burning) shaders — only the demo `dissintegrate`; (10) dithering / palette-swap / LUT colour grading; (11) a .gdshaderinc utility include library (SDF, noise, easing) usable from hand-written shaders, since ShaderV is graph-only; (12) 2D normal-mapped sprite lighting demos. Decals are the one listed sub-domain that does NOT need filling: Godot 4 Forward+ has a native Decal node, and the only notable addon (DecalCo) is Godot 3 only.

RECOMMENDED PRIORITY. GodotRetro alone closes gaps 1, 3 and 10 and is CC0 at Godot 4.7; ultimate-retro-shader-collection is the 4.7 companion for retro spatial materials; GODOT-VFX-LIBRARY closes gap 9 in one drop; Universal-Transition-Shader closes gap 4 (CC0); godot4-cel-shader closes gap 2; the four GDQuest repos close gap 8 but MUST be vendored sparsely because their art is CC-BY-NC-SA.

LICENCE TRAPS FOUND. All four GDQuest repos (godot-shaders, godot-visual-effects, godot-4-VFX-assets, godot-4-stylized-sky) ship an identical dual licence: "1. The demo's source code (script files, scene files, shaders...) is available under the MIT license. 2. Art assets (image textures and 3D models) are CC-BY-NC-SA 4.0". The art is FORBIDDEN under our policy. Sparse checkout of *.gdshader/*.gdshaderinc/*.gd/*.tres only was measured at 1-2 MB per repo and cleanly excludes every texture and model — that is the required vendoring mode, not a nicety. Separately, four otherwise-attractive repos have NO LICENSE FILE and are therefore unusable: GarrettGunnell/AcerolaFX-Godot, GarrettGunnell/Godot-PSX, TheMIU/Stylized-Fluffy-Tree-Shader, CBerry22/Godot-Water-Ripple-Simulation-Shader, marinho/godot-visual-effects. Malidos/Grass-Shader-Example has no LICENSE file either — its README's first line is literally "CC0 MultiMesh Grass Shader for Godot" but there is no formal grant document, so I am treating it as unusable per the hard rule. devkcud/VesperaFX is MPL-2.0 (allowed, flagged). Godot 3-only repos are excluded from vendoring on technical grounds even where MIT: DecalCo, godot_2d_global_illumination, FlexibleToonShaderGD, Godot-Post-Process-Outlines, Godot_BoTW_Toon_Shader, Godot_rain_shader, godot-motion-blur, godot_dither_shader — they use the .shader extension / config_version=4 and need a real port. matmadness/HumanShaders is MIT and excellent but measured 805 MB; link-only.

RENDERER FIT. Everything recommended is Forward+/Mobile-safe for Windows/Linux/Steam Deck. The CompositorEffect repos (GodotRetro, compositor-effect-library) require Forward+ specifically, which we have. Nothing here was assessed on or discounted for browser behaviour.
